CHATGPT PROMPT GUIDE

HOW TO USE CHATGPT
NORMAL PROMPTS & “/prompt” PROMPTS
DETAILED STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE
10 practical examples • Copy • Paste • Customize
For beginners, students, creators, job seekers, and anyone learning ChatGPT.
Important to know: “/prompt” is not an official built-in ChatGPT slash command. It is ordinary text you can
type before your request. ChatGPT mainly follows the instructions that come after it. In most cases, the
normal prompt and the /prompt version below work the same way.
SADDY TECH X
CHATGPT PROMPT GUIDE
Copy • Paste • Customize
PART 1 — THE BASIC METHOD
A. How to use a normal prompt
Step 1: Open the ChatGPT app or website and start a chat.
Step 2: Write your request in everyday language. Example: “Explain gravity in simple English.”
Step 3: Add details: who it is for, how long the answer should be, the style, and the format.
Step 4: Tap Send. For an image, clearly ask ChatGPT to create an image; image-generation availability can depend on
your account and tools.
Step 5: Improve the result by asking for a specific change, such as “Make it shorter” or “Add a labeled diagram.”
B. How to use a prompt that starts with “/prompt”
Step 1: Open ChatGPT.
Step 2: Type “/prompt” at the beginning of your message.
Step 3: Immediately describe your task after it. Example: “/prompt Explain gravity in simple English for Grade 8, with
two examples.”
Step 4: Send the message and read the response.
Step 5: If needed, add a follow-up instruction to improve it.
C. What makes a prompt useful?
TASK
TOPIC
DETAILS
FORMAT
Example: “Create a vertical 4:5 water-cycle infographic for Grade 6, using simple English, labeled arrows, bright colors,
and short explanations.”
When to use which?
Use a normal prompt whenever you want to ask ChatGPT something. Use “/prompt” if you like it as a personal label or
reminder. It does not automatically create a better answer, image, or special mode.
SADDY TECH X

PART 2 — 10 PRACTICAL EXAMPLES
Create an AI Landscape Image
Goal: Make a beautiful image for Instagram or a poster.
NORMAL PROMPT — COPY THIS
Create a realistic vertical 4:5 image of a peaceful mountain lake at sunrise. Add pine trees, misty mountains, a
small wooden cabin, warm golden sunlight, and realistic reflections. Use a cinematic travel-photography style.
“/prompt” VERSION — COPY THIS
/prompt Create a realistic vertical 4:5 image of a peaceful mountain lake at sunrise. Add pine trees, misty
mountains, a small wooden cabin, warm golden sunlight, and realistic reflections. Use a cinematic
travel-photography style.
How to use it:
1. Open ChatGPT and start a new chat.
2. Paste either prompt into the message box.
3. If you want an image, make sure the request clearly says “Create an image.”
4. Send it. If image generation is available, ChatGPT can create the image; otherwise ask for an image prompt.
5. To improve it, say: “Make the colors warmer and add more detail.”
TIP: Both versions give the same instructions; adding “/prompt” does not activate a special tool.
Create an Anime Character
Goal: Create an original character illustration.
NORMAL PROMPT — COPY THIS
Create an original anime character standing in a futuristic city at night. Use glowing blue and pink signs, detailed
streetwear, expressive eyes, rain reflections, dramatic lighting, and a vertical 4:5 composition.
“/prompt” VERSION — COPY THIS
/prompt Create an original anime character standing in a futuristic city at night. Use glowing blue and pink signs,
detailed streetwear, expressive eyes, rain reflections, dramatic lighting, and a vertical 4:5 composition.
How to use it:
1. Choose this example if you want an anime-style image.
2. Copy the complete normal prompt or the /prompt version.
3. Paste it into ChatGPT and send it.
4. If you want a different look, follow up with: “Make it more colorful and use a clean anime art style.”
5. You can also change the character, clothing, colors, or background.
TIP: Describe the subject, setting, style, colors, and aspect ratio.

Make a Product Photo
Goal: Create a professional-looking product visual.
NORMAL PROMPT — COPY THIS
Create a premium product photograph of black running shoes on a clean studio pedestal. Show detailed fabric
and sole textures, soft dramatic lighting, realistic shadows, a minimal background, and a vertical 4:5 layout.
“/prompt” VERSION — COPY THIS
/prompt Create a premium product photograph of black running shoes on a clean studio pedestal. Show detailed
fabric and sole textures, soft dramatic lighting, realistic shadows, a minimal background, and a vertical 4:5 layout.
How to use it:
1. Paste the prompt into ChatGPT.
2. If you have a real product, upload its photo and ask ChatGPT to use it as the reference.
3. Send the prompt and review the result.
4. For an online-store look, ask: “Use a plain white background and keep the product centered.”
5. Check that the product details look accurate before using the image commercially.
TIP: For an existing product, provide a reference photo rather than relying only on a text description.
Design a Technology Logo
Goal: Explore a logo concept for a channel or brand.
NORMAL PROMPT — COPY THIS
Design a bold technology-channel logo for the name SADDY TECH X. Use sharp white lettering, energetic red X
accents, a black background, clean readable typography, and a professional gaming-tech identity.
“/prompt” VERSION — COPY THIS
/prompt Design a bold technology-channel logo for the name SADDY TECH X. Use sharp white lettering,
energetic red X accents, a black background, clean readable typography, and a professional gaming-tech identity.
How to use it:
1. Replace SADDY TECH X with your own brand name if needed.
2. Paste the prompt and send it.
3. Review the generated logo concept.
4. If the lettering is misspelled, ask for a symbol-only version and add the exact text later in a design app.
5. Try another version by changing the colors or style.
TIP: Image generators can make mistakes with text. For a final logo, verify the spelling and consider adding
typography separately.

transport tips, and a budget checklist. Organize the answer by day in a clear table.

1. Use this prompt when you need a travel plan, not an image.
2. Paste it into ChatGPT and send it.
3. Add your travel dates, starting city, number of travelers, and budget for a more useful plan.
4. Ask: “Make the plan suitable for a family with children” or another preference.
5. Verify opening hours, transport, and prices before travelling.
TIP: For planning tasks, tell ChatGPT your dates, budget, location, and preferences.

Explain photosynthesis for Grade 10 students in simple English. Include a short definition, the word equation, a

“/prompt” VERSION — COPY THIS
/prompt Explain photosynthesis for Grade 10 students in simple English. Include a short definition, the word
equation, a step-by-step explanation, key terms, one easy example, and five revision questions with answers.
How to use it:
1. Replace photosynthesis with your own chapter or topic.
2. Paste the prompt and send it.
3. Read the explanation and ask about any difficult word.
4. For exam practice, ask for multiple-choice questions or short-answer questions.
5. Compare important facts with your textbook or class notes.
TIP: Mention your grade, subject, chapter, language level, and exam format.

Goal: Prepare a first resume for a job application.
NORMAL PROMPT — COPY THIS
Help me create a professional one-page resume for an entry-level customer service job. Include a short summary,
relevant skills, education, projects or experience, and editable placeholders for my personal details. Do not invent
qualifications.

/prompt Help me create a professional one-page resume for an entry-level customer service job. Include a short
summary, relevant skills, education, projects or experience, and editable placeholders for my personal details. Do
not invent qualifications.
How to use it:
1. Paste the prompt into ChatGPT.
2. Share only the details you are comfortable providing: education, skills, experience, and target job.
3. Ask ChatGPT to format your information into a one-page resume.
4. Replace all placeholders and check every date and qualification.

3. Review the caption and make sure the details match your post.
4. Ask for a shorter, more professional, or more playful version if you prefer.
5. Copy the final caption into your social media app.
TIP: Tell ChatGPT the platform, audience, tone, goal, and any exact call to action.

Explore Beginner Business Ideas

NORMAL PROMPT — COPY THIS
Suggest five realistic low-cost online business ideas for a beginner. For each idea, list the target audience, basic

/prompt Suggest five realistic low-cost online business ideas for a beginner. For each idea, list the target
audience, basic tools needed, first steps, possible challenges, and a simple way to test demand before spending

How to use it:
1. Paste the prompt into ChatGPT.

3. Pick one idea and ask for a 7-day action plan.
4. Ask what assumptions need testing and what costs you should check.

5. Save the result if you are happy with it.
TIP: Use concrete visual details instead of only saying “make it beautiful.”

This guide brings together all 10 prompt topics from the SADDY TECH X series. Each topic contains 20

1. Open ChatGPT or another AI assistant.

business data or sensitive personal details.

SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 — THE ULTIMATE CHATGPT PROMPT COLLECTION
TOP 100 — THE ULTIMATE

100 Ready-to-Use Prompts for Study, Work, Business, Content, Life & Creativity
100 PROMPTS • 100 USE CASES • 100 EXAMPLES
Published by SADDY TECH X
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 — THE ULTIMATE CHATGPT PROMPT COLLECTION
How to Use This Collection
Each prompt is written as a reusable template. Replace the bracketed or contextual parts with your own information,
then refine the response with follow-up instructions when needed.
Simple formula: Goal + Context + Constraints + Desired Output
Goal
What you want ChatGPT to accomplish.
Context
Relevant background, audience, or situation.
Constraints
Budget, time, length, tone, format, or other limits.
Output
How you want the final answer structured.
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 — THE ULTIMATE CHATGPT PROMPT COLLECTION
Money & Smart Planning
01. /budget
Description: Helps you organize income and spending into a practical monthly budget.
Prompt: Create a monthly budget based on my income, expenses, and savings goal.
Example: Create a monthly budget for an income of I30,000, fixed expenses of I15,000, and a savings goal of
I8,000.
02. /saving
Description: Turns a savings target into monthly or weekly milestones.
Prompt: Create a realistic savings plan to reach [amount] in [time].
Example: Create a plan to save I60,000 in 12 months with a monthly income of I25,000.
03. /expense
Description: Finds spending patterns and highlights areas where costs may be reduced.
Prompt: Analyze these expenses and identify where I can reduce spending: [expenses].
Example: Analyze these monthly expenses: rent I8,000, food I6,000, shopping I4,000, travel I2,000.
04. /shopping
Description: Creates a buying checklist so important features and constraints are not missed.
Prompt: Help me create a checklist for buying [product] based on my budget and requirements.
Example: Create a checklist for buying a laptop under I50,000 for study and video editing.
05. /compare
Description: Creates a structured side-by-side comparison for two choices.
Prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] based on price, features, benefits, drawbacks, and use cases.
Example: Compare Redmi Pad 2 Pro and another tablet based on display, performance, battery, accessories, and
price.
06. /travel
Description: Builds a trip plan with places, timing, transport, food, and practical details.
Prompt: Create a complete travel plan for [destination] for [number] days.
Example: Create a 5-day travel plan for Jaipur for a budget traveler.
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 — THE ULTIMATE CHATGPT PROMPT COLLECTION
07. /itinerary
Description: Turns a destination into a practical daily schedule.
Prompt: Build a day-by-day itinerary for [destination] based on my interests and budget.
Example: Create a 3-day Jaipur itinerary focused on history, food, and low-cost activities.
08. /packing
Description: Creates a destination- and trip-specific packing list.
Prompt: Create a personalized packing checklist for my [trip type] to [destination].
Example: Create a packing checklist for a 7-day winter trip to Delhi.
09. /mealplan
Description: Creates an organized meal schedule around your stated preferences and budget.
Prompt: Create a [7/14/30]-day meal plan based on my preferences and budget.
Example: Create a 7-day vegetarian meal plan with a I2,500 grocery budget.
10. /grocery
Description: Converts meals into a categorized shopping list.
Prompt: Turn this meal plan into an organized grocery shopping list: [meal plan].
Example: Turn this 7-day meal plan into a grocery list grouped by vegetables, grains, dairy, and other items.

11. /routine
Description: Builds a realistic routine around your actual commitments.

Example: Create a weekday routine for studying 4 hours, working 6 hours, and sleeping 8 hours.
12. /timeblock
Description: Assigns specific blocks of time to important tasks.
Prompt: Create a time-blocking schedule for my tasks: [tasks].
Example: Create a time-blocking schedule for study, exercise, content creation, and household work.
13. /habits
Description: Breaks a habit goal into small daily actions and tracking steps.
Prompt: Create a 30-day habit-building plan for [habit].
Example: Create a 30-day plan to build a habit of reading 20 minutes every day.
14. /goal
Description: Transforms a broad goal into measurable milestones.
Prompt: Turn my goal “[goal]” into specific milestones and weekly actions.
Example: Turn my goal of learning Python into 12 weekly milestones.
15. /roadmap
Description: Creates a sequence of stages from starting point to target.
Prompt: Create a step-by-step roadmap to achieve [goal] within [time].
Example: Create a 6-month roadmap to become job-ready in digital marketing.
16. /prioritize
Description: Helps decide what should be done first.
Prompt: Prioritize these tasks by urgency, importance, and impact: [tasks].
Example: Prioritize these tasks: exam revision, email replies, shopping, YouTube video, and bill payment.

Prompt Customization Tips
1. Add your audience: “for a Class 9 student,” “for beginners,” or “for a small business owner.”
2. Add a format: “Use a table,” “give bullet points,” “make a checklist,” or “show an example.”
3. Add constraints: budget, time, word count, tone, platform, skill level, or available resources.
4. Ask for alternatives: “Give me 3 versions,” “show two approaches,” or “include pros and cons.”
5. Review important outputs: ChatGPT can make mistakes, so verify critical facts, calculations, legal/medical
information, and current information.

CHATGPT PROMPTS

SADDY TECH X
PART 1–10 • 100 PROMPTS
COPY • PASTE • CUSTOMIZE • GET BETTER RESULTS
PART 1 • PROMPTS 1–10
1.   /PlanMyDay
Prompt: Create a simple and realistic schedule for my day based on these tasks: [tasks].
Description: Plans your day around your real tasks and available time.
Example: Tasks: study, shopping, exercise. Create a balanced schedule from 7 AM to 10 PM.
2.   /MealPlanner
Prompt: Create a 7-day meal plan using these ingredients: [ingredients].
Description: Creates a simple weekly meal plan from what you already have.
Example: Ingredients: rice, dal, vegetables. Make a 7-day lunch and dinner plan.
3.   /BudgetPlanner
Prompt: Create a monthly budget from my income of I[amount] and expenses of I[amount].
Description: Organizes income and expenses into a practical monthly budget.
Example: Income: I20,000. Expenses: I12,000. Create a budget with savings.
4.   /ShoppingList
Prompt: Create a complete shopping list for my home based on these needs: [items].
Description: Turns your needs into an organized shopping checklist.
Example: Needs: groceries, toiletries and cleaning supplies. Make one categorized list.
5.   /TimeManager
Prompt: Help me organize my day and manage my time better using these tasks: [tasks].
Description: Helps arrange tasks according to priority and available time.
Example: I have 5 hours for study and 2 hours for personal work. Make a timetable.
6.   /CleaningPlanner
Prompt: Create a simple weekly home-cleaning schedule that takes 20–30 minutes per day.
Description: Breaks house cleaning into small daily tasks.
Example: Create a Monday–Sunday cleaning plan for a small home.
7.   /MessageWriter
Prompt: Rewrite this message to sound polite, clear, and friendly: [message].
Description: Makes everyday messages sound more natural and respectful.
Example: Rewrite: “Send me the file quickly.” Make it polite.
8.   /TravelPlanner
Prompt: Create a practical travel plan for [destination] for [number] days within a budget of I[amount].
Description: Builds an itinerary with budget, activities and travel time.
Example: Destination: Jaipur, 3 days, I8,000 budget. Create a practical plan.
9.   /ProblemSolver
Prompt: Help me solve this everyday problem by giving me 3 practical solutions: [problem].
Description: Gives multiple practical options for an everyday problem.
Example: Problem: I keep forgetting important tasks. Give 3 solutions.
10.   /DailyRoutine
Prompt: Create a healthy and realistic daily routine for me based on my schedule: [schedule].
Description: Creates a realistic routine around your existing commitments.
Example: I study from 9 AM–2 PM. Create a routine with meals, exercise and rest.

Description: Creates a beginner-friendly home exercise routine.
Example: Goal: improve general fitness. Make a 4-week no-equipment plan.

Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 1
100 NEXT STUDENT
CHATGPT PROMPTS
Prompts 101–200 • 100 completely new, ready-to-copy prompts
This collection is designed as a continuation of the original 1–100 student prompt collection. The prompts
below focus on new student workflows, analysis methods, writing support, practical learning, project work,
language practice, data interpretation, and study decision-making.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 2
101. /lecture2notes
Prompt: Turn this lecture transcript into structured study notes with headings, key explanations, examples,
and a short takeaway section.
Use: Best for converting a long class lecture into organized notes without losing the teacher's main ideas.
102. /topicgaps
Prompt: Based on my notes for [topic], identify concepts that appear missing or under-explained, then tell
me exactly what I should study for each gap.
Use: Useful when your notes look complete but you are unsure whether important ideas are missing.
103. /questionbank
Prompt: Build a mixed question bank for [chapter] containing recall, application, reasoning, and
higher-order questions. Keep the categories clearly separated.
Use: Creates variety instead of another standard MCQ set.
104. /answerkey
Prompt: Create a detailed answer key for these questions. For every answer, explain why it is correct and
mention the key point a student must include.
Use: Helpful for self-checking after independent practice.
105. /rubricbuilder
Prompt: Create a student-friendly marking rubric for [assignment/question], showing what an excellent,
good, average, and weak response would contain.
Use: Helps you understand what quality looks like before submitting work.
106. /sourcecheck
Prompt: Evaluate these study sources for credibility, relevance, and possible weaknesses. Separate
trustworthy evidence from claims that need verification.
Use: Useful for research assignments and avoiding unreliable information.
107. /citationhelper
Prompt: Show me how to cite the sources I provide for my [assignment] in [citation style]. Keep the format
consistent and flag missing information.
Use: Helps organize citations without inventing source details.
108. /researchquestions
Prompt: Generate 10 focused research questions about [topic], moving from basic investigation to deeper
analysis.
Use: Turns a broad topic into manageable research directions.
109. /researchplan
Prompt: Create a research workflow for [topic] with questions to answer, sources to seek, notes to collect,
and a final synthesis step.
Use: Gives a project a clear research process from start to finish.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 3
110. /sourcecompare
Prompt: Compare these two sources on [topic] for their claims, evidence, perspective, strengths, and
limitations. Do not assume either source is automatically correct.
Use: Useful for source-analysis assignments.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 4
111. /lecturequestions
Prompt: From this lecture text, create questions a student should ask the teacher to clarify confusing,
incomplete, or important points.
Use: Helps turn passive listening into active learning.
112. /classrecap
Prompt: Create a 5-minute verbal recap of today's lesson on [topic] that I can use to explain the lesson to a
classmate.
Use: Good for same-day consolidation after class.
113. /prerequisites
Prompt: Before I study [topic], list the prerequisite concepts I should already understand and give me a
quick diagnostic for each.
Use: Prevents getting stuck because of missing foundational knowledge.
114. /dependency
Prompt: Show the learning dependency chain for [topic]: what I should learn first, what comes next, and
which concepts depend on others.
Use: Useful for subjects with interconnected chapters.
115. /misconception
Prompt: List common misconceptions about [topic], explain why each one is tempting, and contrast it with
the correct understanding.
Use: Targets conceptual errors rather than simple factual mistakes.
116. /edgecases
Prompt: Teach me the important exceptions and edge cases related to [topic], including when the usual
rule does not apply.
Use: Especially useful for mathematics, science, grammar, and programming.
117. /unitconverter
Prompt: Create practice problems that require choosing and converting appropriate units in [subject/topic],
then provide a separate answer section.
Use: Builds practical unit-handling skills.
118. /estimation
Prompt: Teach me how to estimate answers for [type of problem] before calculating exactly, with three
worked examples and practice questions.
Use: Develops number sense and helps catch unreasonable answers.
119. /sanitycheck
Prompt: Show me a systematic way to check whether my final answer to this problem is reasonable without
solving the entire problem again.
Use: Useful for numerical and quantitative subjects.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 5
120. /alternative
Prompt: Solve this problem using two different valid methods and compare when each method is more
efficient or easier to understand.
Use: Builds flexibility instead of memorizing one procedure.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 6
121. /workedexample
Prompt: Create one fully worked example for [concept], then create a similar problem for me to solve
independently without showing the solution.
Use: Provides a model followed by independent practice.
122. /problemselector
Prompt: Given these problems, classify each by the main skill or method required and tell me which one I
should attempt first and why.
Use: Helps students choose an effective practice order.
123. /stepcheck
Prompt: Break my solution into individual steps and label each step as correct, incomplete, or incorrect.
Explain only the first point that needs fixing before moving forward.
Use: Creates targeted feedback instead of rewriting the whole solution.
124. /calculatorlogic
Prompt: Explain which parts of this calculation should be done mentally, on paper, or with a calculator, and
why.
Use: Improves calculator discipline and mathematical reasoning.
125. /graphreader
Prompt: Teach me how to extract information from this graph, including trends, comparisons, unusual
points, and conclusions supported by the data.
Use: Useful for science, economics, geography, and statistics.
126. /tableanalysis
Prompt: Analyze this data table and identify the most important patterns, comparisons, anomalies, and
conclusions I can responsibly make.
Use: Turns raw tables into evidence-based observations.
127. /datainterpret
Prompt: Give me a step-by-step method for interpreting experimental or survey data from [topic], including
what not to conclude from the data.
Use: Builds careful data interpretation skills.
128. /labprep
Prompt: Prepare me for a school lab on [experiment] by explaining the objective, variables, equipment
roles, procedure logic, observations, and questions I should be ready for.
Use: Helps students understand a practical before entering the lab.
129. /labreport
Prompt: Help me organize my observations from this experiment into a lab-report structure. Do not invent
measurements or results that I did not provide.
Use: Keeps lab reports evidence-based.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 7
130. /variables
Prompt: For this experiment or investigation, identify the independent, dependent, controlled, and possible
confounding variables and explain each choice.
Use: Useful for experimental-design questions.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 8
131. /hypothesis
Prompt: Help me turn this research idea into a testable hypothesis and identify what evidence would
support or weaken it.
Use: Improves scientific reasoning.
132. /experimentdesign
Prompt: Design a simple school-level investigation for [question], including variables, controls, procedure
outline, data to collect, and safety considerations.
Use: Useful for science projects and practical assignments.
133. /evidence
Prompt: For each claim in my paragraph, identify what evidence would best support it and explain whether
my current evidence is strong enough.
Use: Strengthens evidence-based writing.
134. /claimbuilder
Prompt: Help me build a clear claim from the evidence I provide. Separate observation, interpretation, and
conclusion.
Use: Prevents unsupported conclusions.
135. /counterargument
Prompt: Find the strongest reasonable counterargument to my position on [topic], then show me how I
could respond using evidence and logic.
Use: Improves argumentative writing and debate preparation.
136. /argumentmap
Prompt: Map my argument into claim, reasons, evidence, assumptions, counterarguments, and conclusion.
Point out any logical gaps.
Use: Makes complex arguments easier to inspect.
137. /logiccheck
Prompt: Check this paragraph for reasoning problems such as unsupported assumptions, false
comparisons, contradictions, or conclusions that do not follow.
Use: Useful for critical-thinking assignments.
138. /biascheck
Prompt: Analyze this text for possible bias in wording, source selection, framing, or omitted perspectives.
Distinguish bias from factual error.
Use: Builds media and information literacy.
139. /perspective
Prompt: Explain how [topic/event] might be viewed differently by three relevant stakeholders, while clearly
separating perspective from established facts.
Use: Useful for history, civics, literature, and social studies.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 9
140. /ethicalanalysis
Prompt: Analyze this student-level ethical dilemma using at least three ethical perspectives and show
where the perspectives disagree.
Use: Encourages structured ethical reasoning.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 10
141. /literarydevice
Prompt: Find and explain the important literary devices in this passage, quoting only short excerpts and
explaining their effect on meaning.
Use: Useful for literature analysis.
142. /characterarc
Prompt: Trace how the main character changes across this story, identifying turning points, motivations,
conflicts, and evidence from the text.
Use: Creates a focused character analysis.
143. /themeevidence
Prompt: Identify the central themes in this text and list specific moments that support each theme. Avoid
treating a topic as automatically being a theme.
Use: Helps distinguish theme from subject matter.
144. /passageanalysis
Prompt: Analyze this passage for tone, purpose, context, word choice, and implied meaning, then give me
three questions I should consider.
Use: Useful for unseen passages and close reading.
145. /poetry
Prompt: Analyze this poem for imagery, structure, sound, speaker, and central idea, explaining how the
techniques work together.
Use: Provides a multi-angle poetry analysis.
146. /bookdiscussion
Prompt: Create a discussion guide for [book/chapter] with open-ended questions about choices, themes,
conflicts, and interpretations.
Use: Useful for book clubs and classroom discussions.
147. /languagepractice
Prompt: Create a short dialogue in [language] for a student at [level], followed by vocabulary notes and
comprehension checks.
Use: Provides contextual language practice.
148. /speakingpractice
Prompt: Conduct a simulated everyday conversation about [situation]. Ask one question at a time and
correct only the most important communication errors.
Use: Builds practical speaking confidence.
149. /pronunciation
Prompt: For these [language] words, provide simple pronunciation guidance, stress patterns, and common
pronunciation mistakes.
Use: Useful for language learners who need pronunciation support.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 11
150. /sentencepatterns
Prompt: Teach me five reusable sentence patterns for expressing [function] in [language], with examples
and short practice tasks.
Use: Helps students produce sentences rather than memorize isolated words.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 12
151. /vocabcontext
Prompt: Create a short story using these vocabulary words naturally, then ask me questions that require
me to infer their meanings from context.
Use: Makes vocabulary learning contextual.
152. /wordfamilies
Prompt: For each word I provide, show useful related forms such as noun, verb, adjective, and adverb
where applicable, with example sentences.
Use: Expands vocabulary efficiently.
153. /readingstrategy
Prompt: Give me a strategy for reading this difficult academic text efficiently, including what to preview,
annotate, and revisit.
Use: Useful for dense textbooks and academic articles.
154. /annotation
Prompt: Show me what kinds of information I should annotate in this passage and provide a compact
annotation key I can reuse.
Use: Creates a consistent reading system.
155. /assignmentdecode
Prompt: Break down this assignment instruction into deliverables, constraints, evaluation criteria, and a
step-by-step action list.
Use: Helps students understand what an assignment actually requires.
156. /requirements
Prompt: Read these assignment requirements and create a checklist of every requirement I must satisfy
before submission.
Use: Reduces missed instructions.
157. /draftplanner
Prompt: Create a drafting plan for my [assignment] with a recommended order for writing sections and a
final revision sequence.
Use: Useful when students do not know where to start writing.
158. /paragraphbuilder
Prompt: Help me construct one strong academic paragraph from my notes using a clear point, evidence,
explanation, and closing link.
Use: Teaches paragraph structure without writing an entire assignment.
159. /transition
Prompt: Suggest logical transition strategies between these paragraphs and explain the relationship each
transition should communicate.
Use: Improves flow and coherence.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 13
160. /concise
Prompt: Reduce this answer to the shortest version that still preserves every essential idea required by the
question.
Use: Useful when answers are too long or repetitive.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 14
161. /expand
Prompt: Expand my short answer by identifying which important ideas are missing, then suggest where
each addition should fit.
Use: Helps develop incomplete answers without unnecessary filler.
162. /tonecheck
Prompt: Review this academic response for tone and tell me which phrases sound too casual, vague,
emotional, or overly complicated.
Use: Improves academic communication.
163. /plagiarismrisk
Prompt: Review my draft for phrases that sound unusually close to the source text and suggest ways to
express those ideas independently without changing the meaning.
Use: Encourages original wording and responsible paraphrasing.
164. /paraphrasepractice
Prompt: Give me a short source passage and ask me to paraphrase it. Then compare my version for
meaning, originality, and unnecessary copying.
Use: Builds real paraphrasing skill through practice.
165. /studyenvironment
Prompt: Help me design a practical study environment for [subject] using my available space, materials,
device access, and likely distractions.
Use: Turns a study space into a more usable learning setup.
166. /deviceworkflow
Prompt: Create a simple workflow for using my phone or computer to study [subject] while minimizing
unnecessary notifications and app switching.
Use: Useful for students who study digitally.
167. /fileorganization
Prompt: Design a folder and file-naming system for organizing my school subjects, notes, assignments,
projects, and revision materials.
Use: Prevents digital study materials from becoming messy.
168. /notetemplate
Prompt: Create a reusable note-taking template for [subject] that includes concepts, examples, questions,
evidence, and follow-up tasks.
Use: Provides a consistent structure for future notes.
169. /flashcardquality
Prompt: Review these flashcards and identify cards that are too vague, contain multiple facts, or would be
difficult to recall. Suggest improved versions.
Use: Improves the quality of existing flashcards.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 15
170. /memorypalace
Prompt: Teach me how to build a simple memory-palace route for remembering [list/topic], then
demonstrate it with a small example.
Use: Introduces a different memorization technique without repeating mnemonic prompts.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 16
171. /visualstudy
Prompt: Convert [topic] into a visual learning plan describing what should be represented as a diagram,
flowchart, timeline, table, or labeled illustration.
Use: Helps students choose the right visual format.
172. /diagramlabels
Prompt: Create a labeling practice exercise for the important parts of [diagram/topic], followed by a
separate answer key.
Use: Useful for biology, geography, physics, and technical subjects.
173. /processflow
Prompt: Turn this process into a numbered flow sequence with inputs, transformations, outputs, and
important decision points.
Use: Clarifies multi-step systems.
174. /causeeffect
Prompt: Build a cause-and-effect chain for [event/process], showing immediate causes, deeper causes,
consequences, and feedback effects.
Use: Useful for history, science, economics, and social studies.
175. /decisiontree
Prompt: Create a decision tree that helps me choose the correct method or concept for solving different
types of [subject] questions.
Use: Turns method selection into a repeatable process.
176. /classification
Prompt: Create a classification framework for [topic] with categories, defining features, examples, and
borderline cases.
Use: Useful when a subject requires distinguishing similar concepts.
177. /patternspotting
Prompt: Give me examples that help me discover the underlying pattern in [topic] before explaining the
rule.
Use: Encourages discovery-based learning.
178. /reverseproblem
Prompt: Give me the final result first and create a problem that could logically lead to that result. Then
explain the reasoning.
Use: Develops reverse-engineering skills.
179. /missingstep
Prompt: Show me a worked solution with one important step removed and ask me to determine what
belongs there before revealing the explanation.
Use: Creates focused practice on reasoning between steps.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 17
180. /errorprediction
Prompt: Before I solve these problems, predict the most likely mistake a student might make on each type
and explain how to avoid it.
Use: Builds awareness of common failure points before practice.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 18
181. /studydecision
Prompt: Given my available study time, exam date, current confidence, and topic list, help me choose what
to study now and explain the trade-offs.
Use: Supports realistic study decisions when time is limited.
182. /catchup
Prompt: Create a catch-up sequence for a student who missed several lessons on [subject], starting with
the minimum knowledge needed to rejoin the current topic.
Use: Useful after absence or missed classes.
183. /backlog
Prompt: Help me turn this backlog of unfinished school tasks into a manageable sequence using urgency,
effort, dependencies, and deadlines.
Use: Prioritizes unfinished work systematically.
184. /deadlineplan
Prompt: Create a backward plan from my [assignment/exam] deadline, including milestones, buffer time,
and a final quality check.
Use: Useful for avoiding last-day completion.
185. /buffer
Prompt: Add realistic buffer time to this study or assignment schedule and explain which tasks are most
likely to take longer than expected.
Use: Makes plans more resilient.
186. /weeklycapacity
Prompt: Estimate how much study work I can realistically fit into this week from the time blocks I provide,
then help me choose priorities.
Use: Prevents overloading a timetable.
187. /habitdesign
Prompt: Design a small study habit for [goal] using a clear trigger, tiny starting action, and simple progress
signal.
Use: Focuses on making studying easier to start.
188. /restart
Prompt: Create a 20-minute restart routine for getting back into studying after a long break, including one
easy task and one meaningful task.
Use: Useful when restarting feels difficult.
189. /energyplan
Prompt: Help me match different types of academic tasks to my high-, medium-, and low-energy periods
based on the schedule I provide.
Use: Uses available energy intelligently without requiring a perfect timetable.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 19
190. /commutelearning
Prompt: Suggest safe, screen-light study activities for learning [topic] during a commute or waiting period.
Use: Useful for turning small spare-time windows into learning opportunities.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 20
191. /grouproles
Prompt: For a group assignment on [topic], divide responsibilities into clearly defined roles with
deliverables, handoff points, and accountability checks.
Use: Improves coordination in group projects.
192. /meetingagenda
Prompt: Create a short agenda for a student group meeting about [project], including decisions to make,
progress updates, blockers, and next actions.
Use: Keeps project meetings focused.
193. /peerfeedback
Prompt: Create a constructive peer-feedback form for [assignment] with specific questions about strengths,
clarity, evidence, and improvement opportunities.
Use: Makes peer review more useful and respectful.
194. /feedbackquestions
Prompt: Give me five specific questions I can ask my teacher about my work to get feedback that is
actionable rather than simply asking whether it is good.
Use: Helps students get better feedback from teachers.
195. /vivaquestions
Prompt: Generate viva questions for [project/topic] in three categories: factual understanding, reasoning,
and questions about my own choices.
Use: Prepares students for deeper oral questioning.
196. /mockdefense
Prompt: Act as a strict but fair project evaluator. Ask me one question at a time about my project, challenge
weak answers, and summarize my strongest improvement areas at the end.
Use: Simulates a project defense or oral assessment.
197. /careerexplorer
Prompt: For my interests in [area], suggest several possible study or career directions and list the
school-level skills I could start developing for each.
Use: Connects current learning with possible future directions.
198. /skillproject
Prompt: Design a small portfolio-worthy project that lets me demonstrate [skill] using tools and resources
suitable for a student.
Use: Turns a skill into a concrete project.
199. /learningaudit
Prompt: Review my answers, notes, and study activity from this week and identify what I can demonstrate
confidently, what is uncertain, and what needs fresh practice.
Use: Creates a evidence-based learning audit rather than a generic reflection.
Saddy Tech X • 100 Next Student ChatGPT Prompts • Page 21
200. /personalstudycoach
Prompt: Using the study information I provide, create a practical next-session plan with one learning
objective, one active task, one application task, and one measurable finish point.
Use: Creates a focused study session tailored to the information I provide.

title: 3.4 Top 100 PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS
summary: TOP 100 PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS For Undergraduate & Postgraduate Study • Simple Explanations • Examples
raw:
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS
SADDY TECH X
TOP 100
PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS
For Undergraduate & Postgraduate Study • Simple Explanations • Examples
For students studying physiology at introductory, undergraduate and postgraduate levels.
HOW TO USE THIS PDF
1. Choose a prompt that matches your topic.
2. Copy the full prompt and paste it into ChatGPT.
3. Replace words inside [SQUARE BRACKETS] with your topic, course level or question.
4. Add lecture notes, a diagram or a research paper if you want the answer to follow that material.
5. Ask for simpler language, more detail, a table, a diagram guide or extra questions when needed.
6. Check important facts against your course textbook, lecturer and current academic sources.
Choosing the level: Use “undergraduate” for basic explanations and core mechanisms. Use “postgraduate” for deeper mechanisms, research
evidence, critical evaluation and advanced discussion. Follow your institution's exact syllabus.
Example: Replace [TOPIC] with “cardiac cycle” and set the level to “undergraduate”. For a deeper answer, use “postgraduate” and ask for
research evidence and limitations.
Study note: This PDF is for education and exam preparation, not personal diagnosis or treatment. For clinical decisions, use qualified medical
guidance.
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS
PART 1 — UNDERSTANDING PHYSIOLOGY BASICS
Each prompt includes what to ask ChatGPT and a simple example of the answer you can request.
1. Explain a physiology topic simply
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain [TOPIC] in very simple language for an undergraduate student. Start with a short definition, explain how it
works step by step, give one everyday example, and finish with 5 key points to remember.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Homeostasis. Expected result: a simple definition, how the body keeps internal conditions stable, an everyday
example such as body temperature control, and a short recap.
2. Make detailed study notes
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Prepare clear study notes on [TOPIC] for a [BA-LEVEL/MA-LEVEL] physiology course. Use headings, definitions,
important terms, functions, mechanisms and a short summary. Explain difficult words in simple language.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Cell membrane. Expected result: notes covering structure, transport, membrane proteins and key terms.
3. Explain a process step by step
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain [PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESS] in the correct order. Number each stage, describe what happens, name the
main organs or cells involved, and explain why each stage matters.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Blood clotting. Expected result: a numbered overview of the main stages and the role of platelets and clotting
factors.
4. Compare two concepts
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Compare [CONCEPT A] and [CONCEPT B] in a clear table. Include meaning, location, main function, process,
similarities, differences and one example of each.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Diffusion vs osmosis. Expected result: a comparison table showing how each type of movement works.
5. Explain a difficult term
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain the physiology term [TERM] for a beginner. Give its meaning, where it is used in the body, why it is important,
and one simple example. Avoid unexplained technical words.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Term: Negative feedback. Expected result: a plain-language explanation using body temperature regulation as an
example.
6. Create a concept map
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Create a text-based concept map for [TOPIC]. Put the main idea in the centre, connect related terms with arrows, and
add a short explanation for every connection.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Nervous system. Expected result: a map connecting brain, spinal cord, nerves, neurons and their main roles.
7. Explain cause and effect
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain how [CHANGE OR STIMULUS] affects [BODY FUNCTION]. Show the cause, the steps in the body's
response, the final effect and any feedback control involved.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Example: How does exercise affect heart rate? Expected result: a cause-and-effect chain describing increased
demand and cardiovascular response.
8. Give an everyday example
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Teach [PHYSIOLOGY CONCEPT] using 3 everyday examples. For each example, explain what happens in the body
and connect it to the scientific concept.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Sweating. Expected result: examples involving hot weather, exercise and fever, linked to temperature
regulation.
9. Make a glossary
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Create a glossary of 20 important terms from [CHAPTER]. Give each term a short, accurate definition and one
sentence showing how it is used in physiology.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Chapter: Respiratory system. Expected result: terms such as ventilation, gas exchange, alveoli and oxygen saturation.
10. Summarise a chapter
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Summarise [CHAPTER NAME] for exam revision. Include the main headings, essential mechanisms, important terms,
key examples and 10 quick revision points. Do not leave out major ideas.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Chapter: Digestive physiology. Expected result: a structured revision summary from ingestion to absorption.
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS
PART 2 — CELL, TISSUE & BASIC BODY FUNCTIONS
Each prompt includes what to ask ChatGPT and a simple example of the answer you can request.
11. Explain cell physiology
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain the physiology of a [CELL TYPE]. Describe its structure, main functions, how it gets energy, how it
communicates and how it supports the body.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Cell: Neuron. Expected result: an explanation of the cell body, dendrites, axon and signal transmission.
12. Explain membrane transport
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Teach [MEMBRANE TRANSPORT TYPE] with a simple definition, the direction of movement, whether energy is
needed, and a clear example from the human body.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Active transport. Expected result: an explanation of movement using energy, with the sodium-potassium pump
as an example.
13. Explain action potential
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain the action potential in a neuron step by step. Cover resting potential, depolarisation, repolarisation and the
return to resting state. Define each stage simply.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: a numbered explanation of how an electrical signal travels along a neuron.
14. Explain muscle contraction
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain how [SKELETAL/SMOOTH/CARDIAC] muscle contracts. Include the important structures, role of calcium and
ATP, and the sequence of events.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Skeletal muscle contraction. Expected result: a clear account of actin, myosin, calcium and ATP.
15. Compare body tissues
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Compare epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue. Explain their main features, locations and functions in a
table, using simple examples.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: a table comparing the four basic tissue types.
16. Explain body fluid balance
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain how the body controls water and salt balance. Include the roles of kidneys, hormones and thirst, and give an
example of what happens during dehydration.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: an overview of fluid balance and the roles of ADH and aldosterone.
17. Explain pH regulation
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain how the body keeps blood pH within a healthy range. Describe buffer systems, breathing and kidney function
in simple steps.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: an explanation of chemical buffers, lungs and kidneys in acid-base balance.
18. Explain metabolism
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain [METABOLIC PATHWAY] at [STUDY LEVEL]. State its purpose, where it happens, main inputs and outputs,
key stages and why it matters.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Glycolysis. Expected result: a stepwise overview of glucose breakdown and ATP production.
19. Explain enzymes
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain how enzymes work in the body. Include active sites, substrates, products and the effects of temperature and
pH. Use one physiology example.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: an accessible explanation using digestive enzymes.
20. Make a tissue revision quiz
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Create 15 questions about [CELL OR TISSUE TOPIC]. Mix multiple-choice, short-answer and application questions.
Give the answer key with short explanations after the questions.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Topic: Muscle tissue. Expected result: a quiz on muscle types, structure and function.
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 PHYSIOLOGY STUDY PROMPTS
PART 3 — NERVOUS SYSTEM & SENSORY PHYSIOLOGY
Each prompt includes what to ask ChatGPT and a simple example of the answer you can request.
21. Explain nervous system divisions
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain the central and peripheral nervous systems, including their main parts and functions. Show how sensory input
and motor output are connected.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: a simple overview of the brain, spinal cord, nerves and their roles.
22. Explain synaptic transmission
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Explain how a signal passes from one neuron to another at a chemical synapse. Include the action potential,
neurotransmitter release, receptors and signal ending.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: Expected result: numbered steps describing communication across a synapse.
23. Explain autonomic nervous system

prompts.title: Check and improve my answer
prompts.text:
COPY-PASTE PROMPT: Review my answer to [QUESTION]. Check scientific accuracy, missing points, clarity and structure. Give a score using
this rubric [RUBRIC] and show how I can improve it. Do not add facts without explaining them.
WHAT IT DOES / EXAMPLE: I paste my answer about the cardiac cycle. Expected result: feedback, missing points and an improved model
structure.


Learn • Understand • Revise • Improve
Use these prompts as study helpers. Follow your official course syllabus and verify important scientific details with trusted academic
sources.

100 NEXT CHATGPT PROMPTS
FOR TEACHER
Prompts 101 to 200  •  with ready-to-use examples
How to use
1. Copy any prompt (or the example) and paste it into ChatGPT.
2. Replace this topic with your own topic, class, board, and time available.
3. The more details you add (class level, language, number of students), the better the answer.
PART 1  •  Prompts 101 to 110
101  /lessonhook
PROMPT
Give me creative lesson hooks to grab students' attention for this topic.
EXAMPLE (READY TO PASTE)
Give me creative lesson hooks to grab students' attention for this topic: Photosynthesis (Class 7 Science).
102  /teachingstrategy
PROMPT
Suggest the best teaching strategies to teach this concept effectively.
EXAMPLE (READY TO PASTE)
Suggest the best teaching strategies to teach this concept effectively: Adding fractions with unlike denominators
(Class 6 Maths).
103  /weeklyplan
PROMPT
Create a detailed weekly teaching plan for this subject with clear objectives.
EXAMPLE (READY TO PASTE)
Create a detailed weekly teaching plan for this subject with clear objectives: Class 8 English Grammar (Tenses), 5
periods per week, 40 minutes each.
104  /classnotes
PROMPT
Generate easy and meaningful class notes for this topic.
EXAMPLE (READY TO PASTE)
Generate easy and meaningful class notes for this topic: The Mughal Empire (Class 7 History).

100 POWERFUL
CHATGPT PROMPTS

Ready-to-use prompts with examples to save time, engage

100 PROMPTS • 10 PARTS • COPY • PASTE • TEACH
SADDY TECH X • 100 Powerful ChatGPT Prompts for Online Teaching
2
SADDY TECH X • Learn • Create • Grow
SADDY TECH X • 100 Powerful ChatGPT Prompts for Online Teaching
3
How to Use These Prompts
1. Copy a prompt command and replace the text inside [brackets].
2. Paste it into ChatGPT and add your class/grade, subject, difficulty or lesson context.
3. Review the output and customize it for your students before using it in class.
Tip: The examples are starting points. Change the topic, grade, language or format to fit your
lesson.
PART 1 • PROMPTS 1–10
100 Powerful ChatGPT Prompts for Online Teaching
1. /icebreaker [Topic]
Start your online class with a fun 5-minute icebreaker related to this topic.
Example: “Give me a fun 5-minute icebreaker activity for an online class on the Solar System.”
2. /storyteach [Topic]
Teach this topic through a short, interesting story that students can easily remember.
Example: “Teach Photosynthesis through a short and engaging story for Class 6 students.”
3. /analogy [Concept]
Explain this difficult concept using 5 simple real-life analogies.
Example: “Explain the concept of Fractions using 5 simple real-life analogies.”
4. /misconceptions [Topic]
List the 10 most common misconceptions students have about this topic and explain the correct
ideas.
Example: “List 10 common misconceptions about Earth's rotation and explain the correct ideas.”
5. /thinkpairshare [Topic]
Create a Think-Pair-Share activity for an online class based on this topic.
Example: “Create a Think-Pair-Share activity for an online class on Climate Change.”
6. /exit ticket [Topic]
Create a 5-question exit ticket to check what students learned at the end of the class.
SADDY TECH X • 100 Powerful ChatGPT Prompts for Online Teaching
4
Example: “Create a 5-question exit ticket for Class 7 on Force and Motion.”
7. /differentiation [Topic]
Create separate learning tasks for weak, average, and advanced students on this topic.
Example: “Create learning tasks for weak, average and advanced students on Algebraic Expressions.”
8. /parentupdate [Lesson]
Write a short professional message to parents explaining what students learned in today's online
class.
Example: “Write a short message to parents about today's online class on the Water Cycle.”
9. /gamify [Topic]
Turn this lesson into a fun online game with points, challenges, levels, and rewards.
Example: “Create a fun online game for Parts of a Plant with levels, points and rewards.”
10. /teachback [Topic]
Create an activity where students explain this topic back to the class to demonstrate their
understanding.
Example: “Create a teach-back activity on States of Matter where students explain it in their own
words.”
SADDY TECH X • 100 Powerful ChatGPT Prompts for Online Teaching
5
PART 2 • PROMPTS 11–20
100 Powerful ChatGPT Prompts for Online Teaching
11. /summary [Topic]
Create a clear and concise summary of this topic for quick revision.
Example: “Create a simple and concise summary of Cell Structure for Class 9 students.”
12. /questions [Topic]
Generate different types of questions (MCQ, short answer, long answer) on this topic.
Example: “Create 10 MCQs, 5 short-answer and 5 long-answer questions on The French Revolution.”
13. /visual [Topic]
Suggest creative visual aids, diagrams or charts to explain this topic online.
Example: “Suggest visual aids and diagrams to explain the Human Digestive System.”
14. /discussion [Topic]
Create thought-provoking discussion questions to encourage student participation in an online
class.
Example: “Give 5 thought-provoking discussion questions on the impact of social media.”
15. /case study [Topic]
Create a real-life case study related to this topic with questions.
Example: “Create a real-life case study on Climate Change with 5 questions.”
16. /project [Topic]
Suggest a creative project or assignment for this topic.
Example: “Suggest a creative project for students on Renewable Energy.”
17. /rubric [Activity]
Create a simple and clear grading rubric for this activity.
Example: “Create a grading rubric for a Science Project with clear criteria.”
18. /reflection [Topic]

6
Create reflection questions to help students think about what they learned.
Example: “Create 5 reflection questions for students about their online learning experience.”
19. /resources [Topic]
Suggest additional resources (videos, articles, websites, tools) for this topic.
Example: “Suggest useful resources for students to learn more about Artificial Intelligence.”
20. /lessonwrap [Topic]
Create a short and engaging lesson wrap-up to end the class.
Example: “Create a 5-minute engaging lesson wrap-up for a class on Fractions.”

21. /learninggoals [Topic]

22. /simplify [Concept]
Explain this concept in simpler language for different age groups.
Example: “Explain Photosynthesis for Grade 4, Grade 7 and Grade 10 in simple language.”

Compare two topics and show key differences in a clear table.

summary: TOP 100 ChatGPT Prompts for Primary Teachers
raw:
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS
SADDY TECH X
TOP 100
ChatGPT Prompts for
Primary Teachers
PART 1–10 · 100 COPY-READY PROMPTS
Plan lessons • Create worksheets • Engage students • Teach smarter
HOW TO USE
Replace words in [square brackets] with your subject, topic, class, or grade. Copy a prompt into
ChatGPT and adjust the result to your students’ needs.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS
PART 1 · TEACHING FOUNDATIONS
/lesson plan
Create a detailed lesson plan for [topic] for Class [grade]. Include learning objectives, prior knowledge, teaching-learning
materials (TLM), step-by-step activities, assessment questions, differentiation, and homework.
/simple explanation
Explain [topic] to Class [grade] students in simple, child-friendly language. Use an everyday analogy, three examples,
key vocabulary, and five questions to check understanding.
/worksheet
Create a printable worksheet on [topic] for Class [grade] with 10 mixed questions: multiple choice, fill in the blanks,
true/false, matching, and short answers. Add a separate answer key.
/learning objectives
Write 3–5 measurable learning objectives for a lesson on [topic] for Class [grade]. Use student-friendly 'I can…'
statements and suggest how each objective can be assessed.
/warm-up activity
Suggest a 5-minute warm-up activity to introduce [topic] to Class [grade]. Include materials, teacher instructions, student
steps, and a quick way to check learning.
/homework ideas
Create meaningful, low-cost homework on [topic] for Class [grade] that students can complete independently or with
family support. Include clear instructions and an optional challenge.
/teaching aids
Suggest simple, low-cost teaching-learning materials for teaching [topic] to Class [grade]. List materials, preparation
steps, how to use each aid, and safety tips.
/question bank
Create a question bank on [topic] for Class [grade] with 5 easy, 5 medium, and 5 challenging questions. Include answers
and identify the skill tested by each question.
/lesson recap
Prepare a 5-minute recap of [topic] for Class [grade] using key points, a mini oral quiz, one pair activity, and an exit
ticket.
/teacher reflection
Create a teacher reflection template for a lesson on [topic]. Include what went well, evidence of learning, challenges,
students needing support, and next steps.
PART 2 · CLASSROOM RESOURCES
/practice worksheet
Make a practice worksheet on [topic] for Class [grade] with a gradual increase in difficulty. Include clear instructions,
enough writing space, and a complete answer key.
/lesson summary
Summarize [topic] for Class [grade] in short bullet points. Highlight key terms, important facts, one example, and three
revision questions.
/visual aids
Recommend visual aids for teaching [topic] to Class [grade]. Describe what each visual should show and how the
teacher can use it during the lesson.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS
/doubt clearing
List common questions students may ask about [topic] in Class [grade]. Answer each in simple language and include a
helpful analogy where useful.
/multi-grade lesson
Plan one lesson on [topic] for a multi-grade classroom with activities for Classes [grades]. Explain how to manage
shared teaching and independent tasks.
/reading passage
Write a short, age-appropriate reading passage for Class [grade] about [topic], followed by vocabulary, 5 comprehension
questions, and an answer key.
/math word problems
Create 10 real-life word problems on [math concept] for Class [grade], moving from easy to challenging. Show working
and answers separately.
/activity-based learning
Design a hands-on activity to teach [topic] to Class [grade]. Include objectives, low-cost materials, procedure,
observation prompts, and assessment.
/assessment rubric
Create a simple 4-level rubric to assess [task/project] for Class [grade]. Include criteria, descriptions for each level, and
student-friendly success criteria.
/parent communication
Draft a respectful, positive message to parents about [classroom topic or student progress]. Keep it clear, supportive,
and action-oriented.
PART 3 · ENGAGING SCIENCE & LEARNING
/concept explanation
Explain [topic] in simple language for Class [grade] using real-life examples, a labelled diagram description, key points,
and a short recap.
/real life examples
Give 10 real-life examples of [topic] that primary students can observe in daily life. Add a short explanation and a
question for each example.
/misconceptions
List common misconceptions about [topic] for Class [grade]. Explain why each is incorrect and provide the accurate
concept with a simple example.
/quick revision
Create a one-page revision sheet on [topic] for Class [grade] with key points, important terms, formulas if relevant, and
five quick questions with answers.
/investigation activity
Suggest a safe, low-cost investigation on [topic] for Class [grade]. Include materials, steps, predictions, observations,
conclusion, and safety precautions.
/differentiated resources
Create three versions of a resource on [topic] for beginner, on-level, and advanced learners. Include scaffolded
questions, core practice, and a challenge task.
/exam questions
Generate exam-style questions on [topic] for Class [grade], including MCQs, short answers, long answers, and
application questions. Provide answers and marks.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS
/cross-curricular ideas
Suggest activities connecting [topic] with maths, art, language, and social studies for Class [grade]. Give instructions and
the learning goal for each connection.
/current events connection
Connect [topic] to a suitable real-world event or everyday issue for Class [grade]. Explain the connection in
age-appropriate language and include discussion questions.
/interactive quiz

title: 4.7 Top 100 science prompt for teacher
summary: TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS FOR SCIENCE TEACHERS Copy-and-paste prompts • Descriptions • Example inputs • Ready-to-use prompt instructions
raw:
SADDY TECH X
TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS
FOR SCIENCE TEACHERS
Copy-and-paste prompts • Descriptions • Example inputs • Ready-to-use prompt instructions
WHAT'S INSIDE
100 practical prompts across 10 sections: lesson planning, concept explanations, experiments, worksheets,
assessments, Biology, Physics & Chemistry, Earth & Space, critical thinking, and teacher support.
HOW TO USE
Copy the full prompt into ChatGPT. Replace details in [square brackets] with your class, grade, topic, or curriculum.
Check scientific facts and review all experiment safety instructions before classroom use.
PART 1–10 • 100 PROMPTS • ENGLISH EDITION
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SCIENCE TEACHER PROMPTS
PART 1 — LESSON PLANNING & TEACHING
001. Science lesson plan
Description: Builds a structured lesson with clear objectives, teaching steps, resources, and assessment.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Photosynthesis
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a 40-minute science lesson plan on photosynthesis for Grade 6. Include 3 measurable learning objectives, a warm-up,
explanation, activity, materials, timing, differentiation, and an exit ticket.
002. Simple concept explanation
Description: Explains a science idea in student-friendly language without losing accuracy.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Matter
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain matter to Grade 5 students in simple English. Define it, describe solids, liquids, and gases, give 3 everyday examples,
and end with a 3-question check for understanding.
003. Interactive lesson
Description: Adds student participation and quick checks to a regular lesson.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Electricity
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Plan an interactive 35-minute lesson on basic electricity for Grade 7. Include a starter question, a teacher demonstration, a
pair activity, discussion questions, and an exit ticket. Include safety reminders.
004. Inquiry-based lesson
Description: Helps students investigate a question instead of only memorizing facts.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Plant growth
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design an inquiry-based lesson for Grade 6 around the question: What helps a plant grow well? Include student predictions,
variables to discuss, observations, and a reflection.
005. Differentiated lesson plan
Description: Adapts one learning goal for students at different readiness levels.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Food chains
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a lesson on food chains for Grade 7 with beginner, on-level, and advanced tasks. Keep the core learning objective the
same and include supports, challenge questions, and a short assessment.
006. Weekly unit plan
Description: Organizes a unit across several lessons with a logical progression.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Force and motion
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a five-day unit plan on force and motion for Grade 8. For each day, list objectives, key vocabulary, activities, materials,
and a formative assessment.
007. Lesson hook ideas
Description: Provides engaging introductions that activate curiosity.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — The water cycle
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Suggest 5 safe, engaging lesson hooks for introducing the water cycle to Grade 6. For each hook, explain the materials, what
students observe, and the question it raises.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SCIENCE TEACHER PROMPTS
008. Problem-based lesson
Description: Connects science learning to a realistic challenge.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Clean water
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a problem-based science lesson for Grade 8: a community needs cleaner water. Give the challenge, constraints,
student roles, research questions, deliverable, and assessment criteria.
009. Cross-curricular lesson
Description: Connects science with another subject to deepen understanding.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Weather data
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Plan a lesson connecting weather science with mathematics for Grade 7. Students should read a simple weather table, make
a graph, interpret patterns, and explain their findings.
010. Improve my lesson
Description: Reviews an existing plan for clarity, inclusion, accuracy, and engagement.
Example topic/input: Existing lesson plan
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Review this science lesson plan for scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language, inclusion, safety, and student
engagement. List the 5 highest-impact improvements and then provide a revised version: [paste lesson plan].
PART 2 — CONCEPT EXPLANATIONS & VISUAL LEARNING
011. Explain at three levels
Description: Creates layered explanations for different levels of understanding.
Example topic/input: Grade 4 to Grade 8 — Gravity
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain gravity at three levels: beginner, Grade 6, and advanced. Give one everyday example at each level and identify any
misconceptions to avoid.
012. Compare two concepts
Description: Makes similarities and differences easy to see.
Example topic/input: Plant cell vs animal cell
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Compare plant cells and animal cells in a table. Include structures, functions, similarities, differences, and a short memory tip
for Grade 7 students.
013. Create a concept map
Description: Shows how key ideas connect visually in a text outline.
Example topic/input: Food and nutrition
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a concept map about food and nutrition for Grade 6. Put 'Food and Nutrition' in the center and connect nutrients,
sources, functions, balanced diet, and deficiency diseases. Use short labels and arrows.
014. Use a simple analogy
Description: Makes a difficult idea easier by connecting it to something familiar.
Example topic/input: Electric circuit
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain an electric circuit using a familiar everyday analogy for Grade 6. State where the analogy works and where it is limited
so students do not form misconceptions.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SCIENCE TEACHER PROMPTS
015. Explain a process step by step
Description: Breaks a sequence into manageable stages.
Example topic/input: Digestion
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain digestion for Grade 6 in numbered steps from mouth to small intestine. Include the role of each main organ and finish
with a short recap.
016. Misconceptions and corrections
Description: Identifies common errors and gives accurate corrections.
Example topic/input: Seasons
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
List 5 common student misconceptions about seasons. For each, give the correct scientific explanation and a simple
classroom question that reveals the misconception.
017. Plan a labeled diagram
Description: Gives the labels and notes needed to create a useful science diagram.
Example topic/input: Flower structure
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a labeled-diagram guide for the parts of a flower for Grade 5. List each label, its function, and a one-line drawing
instruction.
018. Everyday-life connections
Description: Connects abstract concepts to things students already know.
Example topic/input: Friction
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain friction through 5 everyday examples for Grade 6. For each example, say whether friction is helpful or unwanted and
why.
019. Science vocabulary glossary
Description: Builds subject vocabulary with concise definitions and examples.
Example topic/input: Ecosystems
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a glossary of 15 key ecosystem terms for Grade 7. For each term, provide a simple definition and one accurate
example.
020. Reading passage with questions
Description: Creates a short reading text plus comprehension checks.
Example topic/input: The Moon
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Write a 250-word science passage about the Moon for Grade 5. Add 5 comprehension questions and an answer key. Use
accurate, age-appropriate language.
PART 3 — EXPERIMENTS & PRACTICAL ACTIVITIES
021. Design a safe experiment
Description: Structures a fair investigation with variables and a conclusion.
Example topic/input: Which paper towel absorbs most water?
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a safe classroom experiment to compare how much water different paper towels absorb. Include materials,
independent and dependent variables, controlled variables, steps, a data table, and conclusion questions.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SCIENCE TEACHER PROMPTS
022. Low-cost hands-on activities
Description: Suggests practical learning with common materials.
Example topic/input: States of matter
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Suggest 5 low-cost, safe hands-on activities for teaching solids, liquids, and gases to Grade 5. For each, list materials, steps,
the concept demonstrated, and a reflection question.
023. Lab worksheet
Description: Creates a ready-to-use recording sheet for practical work.
Example topic/input: Seed germination
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a lab worksheet for observing seed germination. Include the question, hypothesis, materials, procedure, daily
observation table, conclusion prompts, and a teacher note about caring for living things.
024. Identify variables
Description: Helps students distinguish what changes, what is measured, and what stays the same.
Example topic/input: Plant growth and light
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
For an investigation into how light affects plant growth, identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and at least 4
controlled variables. Explain each in student-friendly language.
025. Risk assessment checklist
Description: Encourages safe preparation and teacher review before practical work.
Example topic/input: Simple school experiment
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a classroom risk-assessment checklist for this science activity: [describe activity and materials]. Include possible
hazards, prevention steps, protective equipment if needed, supervision, and safe cleanup. Follow school rules.
026. Observation diary
Description: Creates a structured way to record changes over time.
Example topic/input: Plant growth for 7 days
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a 7-day observation diary for students tracking plant growth. Include daily prompts, a simple measurement table,
space for sketches, and a final evidence-based conclusion.
027. Demonstration with observations
Description: Plans a demonstration and tells students what evidence to notice.
Example topic/input: Light and shadows
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Plan a simple teacher-led demonstration of how shadows change with light position. List materials, steps, what students
should observe, questions to ask, and a clear explanation.
028. Fair-test investigation
Description: Helps students design a test where only one factor changes.
Example topic/input: Which ramp makes a toy car travel farther?
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a fair test to investigate how ramp height affects the distance a toy car travels. Specify variables, repeat trials,
recording table, and how to draw a conclusion from the data.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SCIENCE TEACHER PROMPTS
029. Pre-lab and post-lab questions
Description: Checks prior knowledge and encourages reflection after an experiment.
Example topic/input: Dissolving substances
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Write 5 pre-lab questions and 5 post-lab reflection questions for an investigation about dissolving. Include answers to the
pre-lab questions and prompts that make students refer to their observations.
030. Equipment-free alternative
Description: Preserves the learning objective when specialized materials are unavailable.
Example topic/input: Magnets
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Suggest a safe alternative activity for teaching magnetism if a school has limited equipment. State the learning objective,
materials, procedure, limitations, and questions for students.
PART 4 — WORKSHEETS & CLASSROOM ACTIVITIES
031. Printable mixed worksheet
Description: Creates a balanced worksheet with a separate answer key.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Types of matter
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a printable worksheet on types of matter for Grade 6 with 10 questions: multiple choice, fill in the blanks, matching,
and short answer. Put the answer key in a separate section.
032. Fill-in-the-blanks
Description: Practices important terms and definitions.
Example topic/input: Human body
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Write 10 fill-in-the-blank questions about the human body for Grade 6. Include a word bank and a separate answer key.
033. Matching activity
Description: Pairs terms with their definitions or functions.
Example topic/input: Energy forms
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a matching activity with 12 forms or examples of energy and their descriptions. Mix the order of the answers and
provide the answer key separately.
034. Sorting and classification
Description: Helps students group examples using scientific criteria.
Example topic/input: Vertebrates and invertebrates
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a classification activity where Grade 5 students sort 12 animals into vertebrates and invertebrates. Include clear
instructions, a student table, and the correct classification key.
035. Science case study
Description: Uses a realistic scenario to develop analysis and problem-solving.
Example topic/input: Plastic pollution
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Write a student-friendly case study about plastic pollution in a local waterway. Include a short scenario, evidence students
can interpret, 5 questions, and possible solutions supported by the scenario.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SCIENCE TEACHER PROMPTS
036. Crossword clues
Description: Turns vocabulary practice into a fun review activity.
Example topic/input: Solar system
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create 12 crossword clues about the solar system for Grade 5. Provide one-word or short answers and a numbered answer
key.
037. Station rotation
Description: Organizes a lesson into small-group learning stations.
Example topic/input: Properties of materials
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Plan four learning stations about material properties. For each station include materials, task, time, student recording prompt,
and a quick check. Make activities safe and suitable for Grade 6.
038. Group model-building task
Description: Encourages teamwork and a physical representation of a concept.
Example topic/input: Water cycle model
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a group activity for students to model the water cycle using low-cost materials. Include roles, steps, key vocabulary,

prompts.title: Unit revision test
prompts.text:
Create a revision test for a unit on matter with vocabulary, diagrams, short answers, classification, and real-life applications.
Include a separate answer key and note any answers that may vary.

prompts.title: Biology topic explainer
prompts.text:

questions and answers.

prompts.title: Plant cell vs animal cell
prompts.text:

chloroplasts, and vacuole, with accurate functions.

prompts.title: Explain a life process
prompts.text:

oxygen. Add a simple word equation and a misconception check.

prompts.title: Food chain and food web
prompts.text:

showing energy flow and 5 questions about what happens if one organism declines.

prompts.title: Plant growth investigation
prompts.text:

observation table, and a reminder to avoid unsupported conclusions.

prompts.title: Adaptation and natural selection
prompts.text:
Explain adaptation and natural selection using desert organisms as examples. Distinguish individual adaptation during life
from inherited changes across generations, and include 4 comprehension questions.

prompts.title: Human body systems
prompts.text:
Create a matching worksheet on the digestive, respiratory, circulatory, skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems. Include main
functions and a separate answer key.

prompts.title: Biodiversity activity
prompts.text:

a discussion of why a small survey cannot represent every species.

prompts.title: Ecosystem pollution case study
prompts.text:

evidence-based questions, and realistic prevention ideas.

prompts.title: Biology revision sheet
prompts.text:
Create a revision sheet on reproduction in plants for Grade 8 with key terms, a process summary, a diagram description, 10
practice questions, and answers.

prompts.title: Physics concept explainer
prompts.text:

three practice questions with answers.

prompts.title: Step-by-step physics problems
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Practical physics investigation
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Physical vs chemical change

classification questions and answers.

prompts.title: Separating mixtures

prompts.text:

prompts.title: Particle model
prompts.text:

drawing task, and include 5 questions.

prompts.title: Energy transfer and conservation
prompts.text:

energy transfer from energy being used up.

prompts.title: Chemistry lab preparation
prompts.text:

procedure overview, safety reminders, and a data table.

prompts.title: Water cycle
prompts.text:

examples, and create 5 questions with answers.

prompts.text:

prompts.text:
