prompts.title: School sustainability project
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Human impact on ecosystems

evaluate realistic conservation actions using evidence.

prompts.title: Higher-order thinking questions
prompts.text:

justification, and include a sample answer outline.

prompts.title: Science fair project
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Real-world problem-solving
prompts.text:

recording, redesign, and evaluation criteria.

prompts.title: Interpret sample data
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Claim-evidence-reasoning task
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Science ethics discussion
prompts.text:

prompts.title: STEM engineering challenge
prompts.text:

rules, data recording, redesign time, and reflection prompts.

prompts.title: Community science project
prompts.text:

possible actions, roles, and a presentation outline.

prompts.title: Science news literacy
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Science classroom debate
prompts.text:

students should research, speaking roles, discussion rules, and a reflection task.

prompts.title: Adapt for three levels
prompts.text:

vocabulary support, and an extension task while keeping the same core objective.

prompts.title: Vocabulary and sentence starters
prompts.text:

prompts.title: Enrichment challenge
prompts.text:

design, provide constraints, and include a rubric.

prompts.title: Catch-up lesson
prompts.text:

prompts.text:

Before using AI-generated material
• Check scientific facts and any figures or claims against reliable sources.
• Adapt the language to your students' age and curriculum.
• Follow school safety rules for experiments, field visits, and community activities.
• Do not ask students to handle hazardous waste, unknown chemicals, sharp objects, or unsafe equipment.
• Protect student privacy; do not paste personal student information into prompts.

prompts.title: Natural hazard comparison
prompts.text:
Floods and droughts
Copy-paste prompt: Create a comparison table of [hazard A] and [hazard B] for Grade [X]. Include common causes,
impacts, preparedness, response, and recovery. Use calm, factual language and refer to local official guidance for
safety instructions.

prompts.title: Local environment study
prompts.text:
School campus environment
Copy-paste prompt: Create a local environment study for [place] for Grade [X]. Include observation categories, a
recording sheet, respectful data collection, questions about patterns and problems, and a student report outline.

prompts.title: Environmental news literacy
prompts.text:
A news report about a heatwave
Copy-paste prompt: Create a media-literacy activity using a teacher-provided environmental news item on [topic]. Ask
students to identify the claim, source, evidence, date, missing context, and questions to verify. Do not fabricate news or
statistics.

prompts.title: Source analysis
prompts.text:
A chart about rainfall
Copy-paste prompt: Prepare a source-analysis worksheet for Grade [X] using a teacher-provided [chart/article/photo]
about [topic]. Include observation questions, what the source supports, what it does not show, and how to check
reliability.

prompts.title: Data interpretation
prompts.text:
Weekly temperature observations
Copy-paste prompt: Create 5 data-interpretation questions for Grade [X] using this data: [paste data]. Ask students to
identify patterns, compare values, and propose cautious explanations. Show calculations and do not add data that was
not provided.

prompts.title: Graph activity
prompts.text:
Classroom waste by category
Copy-paste prompt: Turn this environmental data into a student graphing task for Grade [X]: [paste data].
Recommend a suitable graph, provide axis labels and a title, ask 5 interpretation questions, and include an answer key
based only on the supplied data.

prompts.title: Environmental vocabulary
prompts.text:
Climate and weather
Copy-paste prompt: Create a vocabulary list of 15 important terms about [topic] for Grade [X]. For each term provide a
simple definition, one example sentence, and a quick recall question.

prompts.title: Word search and crossword
prompts.text:
Environment vocabulary
Copy-paste prompt: Create an EVS word-search list and a simple crossword clue set for Grade [X] on [topic]. Include
age-appropriate words, clear clues, and a complete answer key.

prompts.title: Flashcards
prompts.text:
Parts of a plant
Copy-paste prompt: Create 20 study flashcards on [topic] for Grade [X]. Each card should have a short question on
the front and a concise accurate answer on the back. Include a mix of facts, examples, and application questions.

prompts.title: Mind map
prompts.text:
Natural resources
Copy-paste prompt: Create a mind map outline on [topic] for Grade [X]. Use one central concept, 5–7 main branches,
short sub-branches, and examples. Format it so students can easily draw it on paper.

prompts.title: Summary notes
prompts.text:
Climate change
Copy-paste prompt: Write one-page summary notes on [topic] for Grade [X]. Include a definition, key ideas, causes or
processes, effects, solutions, 8 key terms, and a 5-question self-test with answers.

prompts.title: Revision timetable
prompts.text:
EVS unit test in one week
Copy-paste prompt: Create a [number]-day revision timetable for a Grade [X] EVS test covering [list topics]. Include
manageable daily tasks, active recall, practice questions, short breaks, and a final review checklist.

prompts.title: Mock test
prompts.text:
Our environment — Grade 6
Copy-paste prompt: Create a [marks]-mark EVS mock test for Grade [X] on [topics]. Include a balanced mix of
question types, marks for each question, clear instructions, a separate answer key, and a marking scheme.

prompts.title: Unit test paper
prompts.text:
Biodiversity — Grade 6
Copy-paste prompt: Generate a unit test on [topic] for Grade [X] for [marks] marks. Include objective, short-answer,
long-answer, and application questions. Show marks, provide an answer key, and align questions to the stated learning
objectives.

prompts.title: Assessment rubric
prompts.text:
Environmental model presentation
Copy-paste prompt: Create a 4-level rubric for assessing a Grade [X] project on [topic]. Include criteria for accuracy,
understanding, creativity, teamwork, presentation, and reflection. Describe each level clearly and assign a total of
[marks] marks.

prompts.title: Project assessment
prompts.text:
Waste reduction project
Copy-paste prompt: Create a project assessment checklist for Grade [X] on [topic]. Assess planning, evidence
collection, teamwork, accuracy, solution quality, presentation, and reflection. Include observable indicators and a
student self-assessment section.

prompts.title: Exit ticket
prompts.text:
Food chains
Copy-paste prompt: Create 5 exit-ticket questions for a Grade [X] lesson on [topic]: one key fact, one explanation, one
application, one misconception check, and one reflection. Add expected answers and a quick way to group students by
need.

prompts.title: Differentiated instruction
prompts.text:
Water cycle — Grade 5
Copy-paste prompt: Adapt a lesson on [topic] for Grade [X] learners who need extra support, learners at grade level,
and advanced learners. Provide accessible instructions, varied task complexity, scaffolds, extension tasks, and fair
assessment options.

prompts.title: Remedial learning plan
prompts.text:
Air pollution — Grade 5
Copy-paste prompt: Create a 5-day remedial plan for Grade [X] students struggling with [topic]. Identify prerequisite
skills, use short explanations and guided practice, include daily checks, provide answer feedback, and define how
progress will be reviewed.

prompts.title: Enrichment activities
prompts.text:
Sustainable living — Grade 6
Copy-paste prompt: Suggest 8 enrichment tasks on [topic] for advanced Grade [X] learners. Include research, design,
problem-solving, real-world application, and presentation choices. Keep tasks achievable and require students to
explain their reasoning.

prompts.title: Inclusive classroom activity
prompts.text:
Biodiversity — Grade 4
Copy-paste prompt: Design an inclusive EVS activity on [topic] for Grade [X]. Offer multiple ways to participate, clear
instructions, accessible materials, vocabulary support, flexible grouping, and alternatives for students who cannot do a
physical task.

prompts.title: Group work plan
prompts.text:
Reduce classroom waste
Copy-paste prompt: Create a cooperative group task on [topic] for Grade [X]. Assign clear roles, provide step-by-step
instructions, define the final product, include individual accountability, and give a simple teamwork reflection form.

prompts.title: Homework with real-life observation
prompts.text:
Water use at home
Copy-paste prompt: Create a safe 15-minute home observation task on [topic] for Grade [X]. Include instructions, a
simple recording table, privacy-respecting options for students who cannot collect home data, and 3 reflection
questions.

prompts.title: Parent involvement ideas
prompts.text:
Waste segregation
Copy-paste prompt: Suggest 8 simple ways parents or caregivers can support EVS learning on [topic] at home. Keep
activities low-cost, optional, culturally adaptable, and safe; avoid asking families to buy special materials.

prompts.title: Community interview
prompts.text:
Local water sources
Copy-paste prompt: Create 8 respectful interview questions for Grade [X] students to ask a willing adult about [topic].
Include permission and privacy reminders, a note-taking template, and a reflection comparing perspectives without
treating one interview as universal evidence.

prompts.title: Green habits tracker
prompts.text:
Saving water and electricity
Copy-paste prompt: Create a 2-week green-habits tracker for Grade [X] focused on [topic]. Include 5 achievable
actions, daily checkboxes, a weekly reflection, and a reminder that students should never take unsafe actions or feel
blamed for circumstances beyond their control.

prompts.title: Sustainable living challenge
prompts.text:
Reducing food waste
Copy-paste prompt: Design a 7-day sustainable-living challenge for Grade [X] about [topic]. Give one realistic action
per day, a tracking sheet, discussion prompts, and alternatives for students whose households have different
resources.

prompts.title: Green career exploration
prompts.text:
Wildlife biologist and environmental engineer
Copy-paste prompt: Create a Grade [X] career exploration activity about environmental careers linked to [topic].
Include 6 careers, what each person does, useful skills, possible study pathways in general terms, and a reflection on
students' interests.

prompts.title: Career and life skills
prompts.text:
Community recycling project
Copy-paste prompt: Create an activity on [topic] that develops teamwork, communication, problem-solving, planning,
and responsible decision-making for Grade [X]. Include a realistic scenario, student roles, deliverable, and reflection
questions.

prompts.title: Presentation outline
prompts.text:
Renewable energy
Copy-paste prompt: Create a 8-slide presentation outline on [topic] for Grade [X]. For each slide provide a title, 3–5
concise points, a visual suggestion, and speaker notes. End with a recap and 3 quiz questions.

prompts.title: Teaching script
prompts.text:
The water cycle
Copy-paste prompt: Write a natural 5-minute teacher script explaining [topic] to Grade [X]. Use simple spoken
language, ask students questions, include pauses for responses, give a real-life example, and finish with a short recap.

prompts.title: Video lesson script
prompts.text:
Protecting biodiversity
Copy-paste prompt: Write a 60–90 second educational video script on [topic] for Grade [X]. Include a hook, 3 accurate
key points, visual directions, simple narration, and a call to action that students can safely follow.

prompts.title: Classroom game
prompts.text:
Environmental bingo
Copy-paste prompt: Create a classroom game to revise [topic] for Grade [X]. Include objective, materials, rules, setup,
sample game cards or questions, answer key, and a way to include students who prefer not to compete.

prompts.title: Quiz game activity
prompts.text:
Natural resources
Copy-paste prompt: Design a 15-minute team quiz game on [topic] for Grade [X]. Provide 15 questions, answers,
scoring rules, tie-breaker, and respectful participation rules. Balance speed questions with reasoning questions.

prompts.title: Creative writing
prompts.text:
A day without plastic
Copy-paste prompt: Give 5 creative-writing prompts on [topic] for Grade [X]. Include choices such as a diary entry,
short story, letter, poem, or future-world description, plus a simple rubric that values ideas and clarity.

prompts.title: Poem or rhyme
prompts.text:
Save trees
Copy-paste prompt: Write an original, age-appropriate poem or rhyme about [topic] for Grade [X]. Keep it easy to
recite, accurate, positive, and suitable for a school activity. Add 3 comprehension questions.

prompts.title: Newsletter
prompts.text:
Our Environment newsletter
Copy-paste prompt: Draft a one-page school newsletter on [topic] for Grade [X]. Include a headline, short factual
article, student activity highlights, practical tips, a quiz corner, and a student contribution section. Do not invent school
events or quotes.

prompts.title: Integrated EVS activity
prompts.text:
Water conservation with Maths, Art, and English
Copy-paste prompt: Design an integrated activity on [topic] for Grade [X] combining EVS with [subjects]. Include
learning goals for each subject, steps, materials, student output, assessment criteria, and accessible alternatives.

prompts.title: Student reflection
prompts.text:
My environment
Copy-paste prompt: Create 10 age-appropriate reflection questions for Grade [X] after studying [topic]. Include
questions about new learning, remaining questions, evidence, personal connections, and one realistic next step.

prompts.title: Learning station rotation
prompts.text:
Five senses and nature
Copy-paste prompt: Plan 4–5 learning stations for a Grade [X] EVS lesson on [topic]. For each station include task,
materials, timing, instructions, expected learning, and a simple recording prompt. Include safety and accessibility notes.

prompts.title: Misconception check
prompts.text:
Weather vs climate
Copy-paste prompt: List 5 common misconceptions students may have about [topic]. For each, explain the accurate
idea in simple language, give a quick demonstration or example, and write one diagnostic question.

prompts.title: Teacher reflection
prompts.text:
A lesson on pollution
Copy-paste prompt: Create a post-lesson reflection form for an EVS teacher who taught [topic]. Include questions
about student engagement, learning evidence, misconceptions, inclusion, pacing, and one specific improvement for
next time.

prompts.title: Lesson observation checklist
prompts.text:
Group activity on biodiversity
Copy-paste prompt: Create a concise classroom observation checklist for a Grade [X] EVS lesson on [topic]. Include
observable indicators for participation, questioning, collaboration, evidence of learning, inclusion, and use of resources.

prompts.title: Annual EVS activity calendar
prompts.text:
Environment-themed monthly activities
Copy-paste prompt: Create a month-by-month EVS activity calendar for Grade [X] aligned to [school year or syllabus].
Suggest one feasible activity per month, likely materials, learning goal, and a note to verify dates and local syllabus
requirements.

prompts.title: Syllabus mapping
prompts.text:
Grade 5 EVS unit on water
Copy-paste prompt: Map these EVS topics and learning outcomes to a teaching plan: [paste syllabus or outcomes].
Create a table with topic, objective, activity, resource, assessment, and estimated time. Do not assume curriculum
requirements not provided.

prompts.title: Resource list
prompts.text:
Teaching biodiversity
Copy-paste prompt: Suggest categories of free or low-cost resources for teaching [topic] to Grade [X], such as books,
local observations, teacher-made diagrams, and safe demonstrations. Explain how each resource supports learning
and remind me to verify availability and accuracy.

Before using AI-generated material
• Check scientific facts and any figures or claims against reliable sources.
• Adapt the language to your students' age and curriculum.
• Follow school safety rules for experiments, field visits, and community activities.
• Do not ask students to handle hazardous waste, unknown chemicals, sharp objects, or unsafe equipment.
• Protect student privacy; do not paste personal student information into prompts.

Want more teacher prompt collections? Follow SADDY TECH X.

title: 4.9 Top 100 Social Science prompt
summary: TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS FOR SOCIAL SCIENCE TEACHERS 100 copy-and-paste prompts • Descriptions • Example topics • Ready-to-use instructions
raw:
SADDY TECH X
TOP 100 CHATGPT PROMPTS
FOR SOCIAL SCIENCE TEACHERS
100 copy-and-paste prompts • Descriptions • Example topics • Ready-to-use instructions
WHAT'S INSIDE
100 prompts across 10 parts: lesson planning, History, Geography, Civics, Economics, culture and society, maps and
source analysis, debates, projects, revision, and assessment.
HOW TO USE
Copy the full prompt into ChatGPT. Replace anything in [square brackets] with your topic, grade, country, source, or
class details. Verify historical facts, current data, and country-specific civic information with reliable sources.
PART 1–10 • 100 PROMPTS • ENGLISH EDITION
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
PART 1 — LESSON PLANNING & SOCIAL SCIENCE FOUNDATIONS
001. Build a Social Science lesson plan
Description: Creates a complete lesson with objectives, activities, resources, and assessment.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Our Earth
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a 40-minute Social Science lesson plan for Grade 6 on [topic]. Include 3 measurable objectives, key vocabulary, a
warm-up, teaching steps, a student activity, resources, differentiation, and an exit ticket.
002. Explain a concept simply
Description: Explains an idea in age-appropriate language with examples.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Community
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain [Social Science concept] to Grade 5 students in simple English. Give a definition, 3 everyday examples, and 4 questions
to check understanding.
003. Create an inquiry lesson
Description: Encourages students to ask questions and investigate evidence.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Why do cities grow?
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design an inquiry-based lesson for Grade 7 around the question '[inquiry question]'. Include prior-knowledge questions, evidence
students can examine, group tasks, and a conclusion activity.
004. Make a weekly unit plan
Description: Organizes a topic across several lessons.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Democracy
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a five-day unit plan on [Social Science topic] for Grade 8. List daily objectives, vocabulary, activities, resources, and
formative assessments.
005. Create a lesson hook
Description: Starts a lesson with a curiosity-building question or activity.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Maps
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Suggest 5 engaging lesson hooks for introducing [topic] to Grade 6. For each, include the question or activity, materials, and how
it connects to the lesson objective.
006. Plan group work
Description: Builds collaboration around a shared task.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Natural resources
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a group activity on [topic] for Grade 7. Assign roles, provide clear steps, set a time limit, and include a short presentation
and reflection.
007. Differentiate a lesson
Description: Adapts the task for different readiness levels.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Climate
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Adapt a lesson on [topic] for beginner, on-level, and advanced learners while keeping the same learning objective. Include
scaffolds and extension tasks.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
008. Connect topic to daily life
Description: Makes abstract ideas meaningful through real-world connections.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Local government
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain how [topic] connects to students' daily lives. Give 5 relatable examples and create a short discussion activity for Grade
[level].
009. Create a cross-curricular task
Description: Connects Social Science with other subjects.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Population data
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a task connecting Social Science with Mathematics and English through [topic]. Include data interpretation, discussion,
and a short writing output.
010. Review a lesson plan
Description: Checks clarity, inclusion, accuracy, and assessment.
Example topic/input: Teacher's draft plan
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Review this Social Science lesson plan for accuracy, age appropriateness, inclusion, engagement, and assessment. Suggest the
five most useful improvements, then rewrite it: [paste plan].
PART 2 — HISTORY & HISTORICAL THINKING
011. Create a historical timeline
Description: Organizes events chronologically and shows change over time.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Ancient civilization
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a timeline of 8 key events related to [historical topic] for Grade 6. Add dates where reliably known, one-sentence
descriptions, and a note when dates are approximate.
012. Cause and effect analysis
Description: Helps students distinguish causes, events, and consequences.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — A historical event
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain the main causes and effects of [historical event] for Grade 8. Separate long-term causes, immediate triggers, and short-
and long-term consequences.
013. Compare two civilizations
Description: Highlights similarities and differences using clear criteria.
Example topic/input: Ancient Egypt and Indus Valley
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Compare [civilization A] and [civilization B] in a table covering location, government, economy, daily life, technology, and legacy.
Avoid unsupported claims and note uncertainty where relevant.
014. Analyze a historical source
Description: Builds evidence-based reading of documents and artifacts.
Example topic/input: A historical letter
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a source-analysis worksheet for [historical source]. Ask students who created it, when, for whom, why, what it reveals, and
what it cannot tell us.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
015. Explain historical change
Description: Shows what changed, what stayed the same, and why.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Trade routes
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain how [historical development] changed society over time. Organize the answer into before, during, after, continuity, and
change.
016. Explore multiple perspectives
Description: Helps students consider how people experienced an event differently.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Industrialization
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a classroom activity exploring different perspectives on [historical event or change]. Include source-based questions and
remind students to distinguish evidence from assumptions.
017. Create a history case study
Description: Turns a topic into a focused investigation.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — A historic city
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Write a student-friendly case study about [historical place or event]. Include a short overview, key evidence, 5 questions, and a
final claim supported by evidence.
018. Historical debate
Description: Encourages respectful argument supported by sources.
Example topic/input: Grade 9 — A policy decision
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Plan a classroom debate about [historical question]. Give students roles, source-research questions, debate rules, evidence
requirements, and a reflection task.
019. Explain a historical term
Description: Defines a term and places it in context.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Empire
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain the historical term [term] for Grade 6. Include a definition, context, example, non-example if useful, and three
check-for-understanding questions.
020. History revision quiz
Description: Reviews chronology, concepts, and evidence.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — A chapter
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a 15-question revision quiz on [history chapter], mixing chronology, key terms, causes and effects, and source
interpretation. Include a separate answer key.
PART 3 — GEOGRAPHY & MAP SKILLS
021. Teach map symbols
Description: Practises interpreting symbols, keys, scale, and direction.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Local map
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a map-skills worksheet for Grade 5 covering symbols, legend, compass directions, and scale. Include a simple
text-described map scenario and answer key.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
022. Explain landforms
Description: Introduces physical geography through definitions and examples.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Mountains and plains
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain mountains, plateaus, plains, valleys, and deserts for Grade 6. Provide definitions, examples, and a matching activity with
answers.
023. Compare climate regions
Description: Connects climate patterns to environments and daily life.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Desert and tropical regions
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Compare [region A] and [region B] by climate, rainfall, vegetation, settlement, and livelihoods. Use reliable facts and distinguish
weather from climate.
024. Create a map-reading challenge
Description: Builds spatial reasoning through a practical task.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Direction and distance
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a map-reading challenge using a fictional town map. Include 6 direction and distance questions, a simple map description,
and an answer key.
025. Explain the water cycle and geography
Description: Connects physical processes with places and people.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — River basin
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain how the water cycle affects [geographic area]. Include precipitation, runoff, infiltration, rivers, and how people depend on
water.
026. Population data activity
Description: Teaches students to interpret population patterns.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Sample population table
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a clearly labeled sample population dataset for three fictional regions. Ask students to compare density, growth, and
settlement patterns, with model answers.
027. Natural resources map
Description: Links resources to location, use, and sustainability.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Resources
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create an activity where students map major types of natural resources in [country or region]. Ask them to explain how location
affects use and trade; suggest checking current official maps.
028. Natural hazards lesson
Description: Explains hazard causes, impacts, and preparedness.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Floods
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a lesson on [natural hazard] for Grade 7, including causes, impacts, preparedness, a case-study task, and advice to follow
local official safety guidance.
029. Urban and rural comparison
Description: Compares settlement patterns and services.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Village and city
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Compare rural and urban settlements in a table covering jobs, transport, services, population, and challenges. Avoid suggesting
one lifestyle is inherently better.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
030. Geography revision sheet
Description: Summarizes vocabulary, diagrams, and map concepts.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — A geography unit
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a revision sheet for [geography unit] with key terms, a concept summary, map skills, 10 practice questions, and answers.
PART 4 — CIVICS, GOVERNMENT & CITIZENSHIP
031. Explain democracy
Description: Introduces core democratic principles and participation.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Democracy
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain democracy for Grade 7 using simple language. Include participation, elections, rights, responsibilities, and a classroom
example.
032. Compare levels of government
Description: Clarifies responsibilities at different levels.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Local, state, national
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a comparison table of local, state, and national government in [country]. Use current, reliable information and label
responsibilities that vary by jurisdiction.
033. Create a mock election
Description: Simulates voting and decision-making in a classroom.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Class representative
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a fair classroom mock election. Include candidate statements, voter education, secret ballot steps, counting procedure,
and a reflection on fairness.
034. Rights and responsibilities
Description: Connects civic rights to respectful participation.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — School community
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a scenario-based activity about rights and responsibilities for Grade 6. Include 5 scenarios, discussion questions, and
model responses.
035. Explain the constitution
Description: Introduces the purpose and structure of a constitution.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Constitution
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain the purpose of a constitution for Grade 8 in [country]. Include key principles, simple examples, and a note to verify
country-specific details from official sources.
036. Civic problem-solving
Description: Helps students propose realistic community improvements.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Waste in public spaces
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a civic action project where students identify a local community issue, gather safe and respectful observations, propose
solutions, and present recommendations.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
037. Classroom rules and fairness
Description: Uses familiar examples to explore rules and justice.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Fair rules
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a classroom discussion activity on why communities need rules. Include scenarios, questions about fairness, and a
reflection on how rules can be improved.
038. Media and citizenship
Description: Builds careful evaluation of civic information.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Public announcement
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a media-literacy activity where students assess a public announcement. Include source, purpose, evidence, audience, and
fact-checking questions.
039. Community services
Description: Shows how public services support daily life.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Public services
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a matching worksheet about community services such as health, sanitation, transport, and education. Include who
provides each service and an answer key.
040. Civics assessment
Description: Checks understanding of institutions and participation.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Civics chapter
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a 15-question civics assessment for [grade and topic] with multiple-choice, short-answer, and scenario questions. Include
answers and mark allocations.
PART 5 — ECONOMICS, WORK & RESOURCES
041. Explain needs and wants
Description: Introduces basic economic choices.
Example topic/input: Grade 5 — Household choices
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain needs and wants for Grade 5 using everyday examples. Create a sorting activity with 12 items and note that context can
affect some choices.
042. Goods and services
Description: Clarifies different kinds of economic activity.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Local market
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain goods and services with examples from a local market. Create a classification worksheet with 12 examples and an answer
key.
043. Supply and demand
Description: Introduces how availability and demand can affect prices.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Fruit market
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain supply and demand for Grade 8 using a fictional fruit market. Include a simple data table and questions about how
changing supply or demand may affect price.
SADDY TECH X  |  TOP 100 SOCIAL SCIENCE PROMPTS
044. Create a household budget activity
Description: Practises planning limited resources and prioritizing spending.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Fictional family budget
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a fictional monthly household budget for a classroom activity. Ask students to classify essential and optional costs, make
choices, and explain trade-offs without judging real families.
045. Trade and interdependence
Description: Shows how places exchange goods and depend on one another.
Example topic/input: Grade 7 — Everyday products
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a lesson about trade and interdependence using everyday products. Ask students to trace possible stages from raw
materials to consumers and discuss benefits and challenges.
046. Types of economic activity
Description: Explores primary, secondary, and tertiary activities.
Example topic/input: Grade 6 — Jobs in a town
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Explain primary, secondary, and tertiary economic activities for Grade 6. Give examples and create a sorting activity with
answers.
047. Natural resources and sustainability
Description: Connects economic choices to environmental limits.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — Forest resources
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a case study about using forest resources sustainably. Include stakeholder perspectives, possible trade-offs, and
evidence-based discussion questions.
048. Entrepreneurship project
Description: Encourages planning a simple, ethical business idea.
Example topic/input: Grade 8 — School fair stall
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Design a classroom entrepreneurship project for a school fair stall. Include a product idea, fictional costs, pricing, roles, ethical
considerations, and reflection.
049. Poverty and inequality discussion
Description: Encourages sensitive, evidence-based exploration of social and economic issues.
Example topic/input: Grade 9 — Access to services
COPY & PASTE PROMPT:
Create a respectful classroom activity about unequal access to services. Use a fictional scenario, avoid stereotypes, and ask
students to consider structural factors and possible responses.
050. Economics revision quiz
Description: Reviews key terms and application.

PART 8 — DEBATES, CASE STUDIES & REAL-WORLD LEARNING

prompts.title: Classroom debate
prompts.text:
Plan a classroom debate on [Social Science question]. Include balanced viewpoints, research questions, speaking roles, evidence
rules, respectful discussion norms, and a reflection task.

prompts.title: Analyze statistics
prompts.text:
Create a clearly labeled fictional statistics table about [topic]. Write 6 questions about comparisons, trends, percentages if
appropriate, and what the data cannot prove.

prompts.title: Social Science case study
prompts.text:
Write a student-friendly case study about [community issue]. Include context, a short data table, stakeholder perspectives, 5
analysis questions, and possible solutions.

prompts.title: Compare political systems
prompts.text:
Compare [political systems] using neutral criteria such as executive selection, legislature, accountability, and decision-making.
Note that real systems vary and use reliable sources.

prompts.title: Mock election or council meeting
prompts.text:
Create a classroom simulation of a council meeting about a proposed community park. Include stakeholder roles, agenda,
evidence cards, discussion rules, and a final decision process.

prompts.title: Cause and effect
prompts.text:
Analyze the causes and effects of [Social Science issue]. Organize long-term factors, immediate triggers, short-term effects, and
long-term consequences. Ask students to support claims with evidence.

prompts.title: Current events analysis
prompts.text:
Create a current-events analysis template for students. Ask them to record the date, source, key facts, evidence, perspectives,
and unanswered questions. Verify current details with reliable reporting.

prompts.title: Community problem-solving
prompts.text:
Design a student civic project about [local issue]. Include safe observation, stakeholder questions, evidence collection, realistic
proposals, and a presentation plan.

prompts.title: Perspective taking
prompts.text:
Create a role-based activity exploring how different community members may view [public issue]. Use fictional roles, include
varied priorities, and ask students to distinguish perspective from fact.

prompts.title: Unit review challenge
prompts.text:
Create an end-of-unit review challenge for [Social Science unit] with vocabulary, source analysis, map or data interpretation, short
answers, and one real-world application task.

PART 9 — CRITICAL THINKING, PROJECTS & PRESENTATIONS

prompts.title: Create an infographic assignment
prompts.text:
Design an infographic assignment on [topic]. Include research questions, required facts, source-checking rules, layout
suggestions, and a rubric for accuracy and clarity.

prompts.title: Generate discussion questions
prompts.text:
Create 12 open-ended discussion questions about [topic] for Grade 8. Include factual, comparative, ethical, and evidence-based
questions.

prompts.title: Historical event analysis
prompts.text:
Create an analysis guide for [historical event] covering context, causes, key evidence, multiple perspectives, consequences, and
what remains uncertain.

prompts.title: Compare two places or societies
prompts.text:
Create a comparison table for [place or society A] and [place or society B]. Compare geography, economy, culture, governance,
and daily life without stereotyping.

prompts.title: Primary-source investigation
prompts.text:
Create a primary-source investigation using this teacher-provided excerpt: [paste source]. Ask about author, context, audience,
purpose, evidence, and limitations.

prompts.title: Map activity project
prompts.text:
Design a map-making project about [place or theme]. Include map title, legend, symbols, direction, scale where appropriate, and a
short explanation of patterns.

prompts.title: Social issue research project
prompts.text:
Create a research project on [social issue]. Include a research question, credible source criteria, outline, evidence table, respectful
language guidance, and presentation rubric.

prompts.title: Role-play scenario
prompts.text:
Create a role-play activity about [civic or economic issue]. Include roles, scenario cards, decision options, rules, and a debrief
connecting the simulation to real concepts.

prompts.title: Real-world connection task
prompts.text:
Create a real-world application task for [topic]. Students should observe or analyze a teacher-approved example, use evidence,
suggest actions, and reflect on limitations.

prompts.title: Student presentation rubric
prompts.text:
Create a four-level rubric for a Social Science presentation assessing accuracy, evidence, organization, visual clarity, respectful
language, and responses to questions.
PART 10 — REVISION, ASSESSMENT & TEACHER SUPPORT

prompts.title: Create a revision guide
prompts.text:
Turn these Social Science notes into a revision guide with headings, key terms, examples, and 15 self-test questions with
answers: [paste notes].

prompts.title: Mixed-format quiz
prompts.text:
Create a 20-question quiz on [topic] with multiple-choice, matching, short-answer, map or data interpretation, and one reasoning
question. Include a separate answer key.

prompts.title: Different difficulty levels
prompts.text:
Create beginner, intermediate, and advanced questions on [topic]. Keep the core learning objective the same and include
answers or marking guidance.

prompts.title: Short-answer practice
prompts.text: Write 10 short-answer questions on [topic]. Provide model answers of the requested length and a simple marking guide.

prompts.title: Long-answer response structure
prompts.text:
Teach students how to write a structured long answer on [topic]. Include an opening statement, organized points, supporting
evidence, conclusion, a model outline, and a marking checklist.

prompts.title: Assessment rubric
prompts.text:
Create a four-level rubric for a Social Science research assignment. Assess question quality, source use, evidence, explanation,
organization, and referencing.

prompts.title: Remedial learning plan
prompts.text:
Create a one-week remedial plan for students struggling with [Social Science skill]. Include a short diagnostic, daily mini-lessons,
guided practice, and progress checks.

prompts.title: Enrichment activities
prompts.text:
Suggest 5 enrichment activities for students who have mastered [topic]. Focus on research, comparison, data analysis, and
evidence-based reasoning.

prompts.title: Homework and project ideas
prompts.text:
Suggest 5 homework or mini-project options for [topic]. Include learning goals, steps, expected output, assessment criteria, and
alternatives that do not require internet access.

prompts.title: Review my unit plan
prompts.text:
Review this Social Science unit plan for accuracy, balanced perspectives, inclusion, skill development, and assessment. Suggest
five improvements and provide a revised outline: [paste unit plan].

• Replace all bracketed placeholders before submitting the prompt.

QUICK TIPS FOR TEACHERS
• Replace all bracketed placeholders before submitting the prompt.
• Review generated instructions and code before using them with students.
• Do not enter real student passwords or sensitive personal information into AI tools.
• Test code and software steps in a safe, supervised environment.
• Adapt tasks for student skill levels and local curriculum requirements.
• Encourage students to explain their own thinking, not just copy generated answers.

Drawing lessons • Painting • Colour theory • Craft projects • Art history • Worksheets •

Replace the [bracketed text] with your topic, grade level, or materials. Copy the prompt into ChatGPT,

TEACH • CREATE • EMPOWER
SADDY TECH X  •  ART & DRAWING TEACHER PROMPTS
PART 1 — PROMPTS 1–10
1. Art lesson plan
Use: Plan a structured art lesson with objectives, materials, demonstration, practice, and assessment.
Example: Watercolour landscapes, Grade 5
Copy-paste prompt: Create a 40-minute art lesson plan for [topic] for [grade level]. Include learning objectives, materials,
teacher demonstration, step-by-step student activity, differentiation, and a simple assessment checklist.
2. Step-by-step drawing
Use: Break a drawing into easy shapes and stages for beginners.
Example: A cat using circles and ovals, Grade 2
Copy-paste prompt: Teach students how to draw [object] step by step for [grade level]. Begin with basic shapes, give clear
numbered steps, explain proportions, and finish with simple colouring tips.
3. Shape-based drawing
Use: Use basic shapes to help young learners draw confidently.
Example: House using squares, rectangles, and triangles
Copy-paste prompt: Create a beginner-friendly drawing activity using circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles to draw
[subject] for [grade level]. Include steps and a quick practice task.
4. Line art practice
Use: Build control with straight, curved, zigzag, and wavy lines.
Example: Line patterns for Grade 1
Copy-paste prompt: Design a line-art worksheet for [grade level] that practises straight, curved, zigzag, wavy, and spiral
lines. Include instructions, a progression from easy to challenging, and teacher tips.
5. Colour wheel activity
Use: Teach primary, secondary, and tertiary colours through practice.
Example: Primary and secondary colours, Grade 4
Copy-paste prompt: Create a colour-wheel activity for [grade level]. Explain primary, secondary, and tertiary colours, list
materials, provide steps, and add five quick understanding questions.
6. Warm and cool colours
Use: Help students identify colour temperature and mood.
Example: Warm sunset and cool winter scene
Copy-paste prompt: Plan an art activity that teaches warm and cool colours to [grade level]. Include examples, a two-panel
drawing task, reflection questions, and a simple rubric.
SADDY TECH X  •  ART & DRAWING TEACHER PROMPTS
7. Shading basics
Use: Teach light, shadow, and tonal value with pencil.
Example: Shading a sphere, Grade 6
Copy-paste prompt: Explain pencil shading to [grade level] using a sphere as the example. Include light source, highlight,
midtone, core shadow, reflected light, cast shadow, and a step-by-step practice task.
8. Texture drawing
Use: Explore visual texture through marks and patterns.
Example: Bark, fur, stone, and leaves
Copy-paste prompt: Create a texture drawing lesson for [grade level]. Include at least eight textures students can draw using
different lines, dots, hatching, and stippling, plus a practice grid.
9. Still-life drawing
Use: Teach observation, proportions, and composition.
Example: Cup, apple, and book
Copy-paste prompt: Plan a still-life drawing lesson using [objects] for [grade level]. Explain observation, basic shapes,
proportion, placement, light and shadow, and provide a peer-feedback checklist.
10. Nature drawing
Use: Observe natural forms and draw them accurately.
Example: Leaves, flowers, and seed pods
Copy-paste prompt: Design a nature-drawing activity for [grade level] using leaves, flowers, or seed pods. Include
observation prompts, shape and vein details, safe material handling, and a reflection task.
SADDY TECH X  •  ART & DRAWING TEACHER PROMPTS
PART 2 — PROMPTS 11–20
11. Animal drawing
Use: Simplify animal anatomy into beginner-friendly forms.
Example: Butterfly, Grade 3
Copy-paste prompt: Create a step-by-step animal drawing guide for [animal] suitable for [grade level]. Use simple shapes,
explain key features, and add optional details for students who finish early.
12. Bird drawing
Use: Teach feather patterns, beaks, and body proportions.
Example: Sparrow on a branch
Copy-paste prompt: Write an easy drawing tutorial for [bird] for [grade level]. Break the body into simple shapes and explain
the beak, wings, tail, feet, and a natural background.
13. Human figure basics
Use: Introduce gesture, proportion, and simple poses.
Example: Standing figure, Grade 7
Copy-paste prompt: Create an age-appropriate lesson on drawing a simple human figure for [grade level]. Explain gesture

• Replace all bracketed placeholders before submitting the prompt.
• Review generated art instructions for age suitability and classroom safety.
• Encourage original ideas and personal interpretation instead of requiring identical copies.

SADDY TECH X • Educational Infographic Prompts
TOP 100 EDUCATIONAL
INFOGRAPHIC PROMPTS
100 copy-ready prompts with visual output examples
Created for SADDY TECH X
HOW TO USE THIS PDF
1. Choose a topic and copy its prompt. 2. Paste it into ChatGPT or your preferred AI image tool. 3. Change details such as
country, grade level, or style when needed. 4. Check facts, spelling, and labels before posting.
Slash-style labels such as /solar system are convenient topic tags to type at the start of a request; they are not official ChatGPT
commands.
Every entry includes a ready-to-copy prompt and a short visual example to guide the result.

PART 1 — STARTER CLASSROOM VISUALS
SADDY TECH X   |   Copy-and-paste prompt collection   |   10 prompts
001. /FLASHCARD
Copy prompt: Create a colorful educational flashcard for [WORD/TOPIC]. Show one clear illustration, the word in large
readable text, a simple definition, and one example sentence. Use a clean classroom-friendly layout suitable for [GRADE].
002. /VOCAB
Copy prompt: Create a vocabulary learning card for the word [WORD]. Include a simple picture, pronunciation guide,
child-friendly meaning, one synonym, and an example sentence. Keep the spelling accurate and the design easy to read.
003. /STORY
Copy prompt: Create a story-writing prompt from this image idea: [SCENE]. Show a clear, age-appropriate scene and add
three questions: Who is there? What is happening? What might happen next? Leave space for students to write.
004. /SEQUENCE
Copy prompt: Create a picture-sequencing worksheet about [PROCESS/STORY]. Show four clear stages in mixed order,
with numbered blank boxes so students can arrange them from beginning to end. Keep the illustrations consistent.
005. /COMPREHENSION
Copy prompt: Create a reading-comprehension activity about [TOPIC] for [GRADE]. Include a short age-appropriate
passage, one relevant illustration, and five questions with space for answers. Use simple language and accurate facts.
006. /GRAMMAR
Copy prompt: Create a grammar correction visual for [GRAMMAR RULE]. Show one incorrect sentence and its corrected
version, highlight the change, and add a short explanation plus two practice examples.
007. /LABEL
Copy prompt: Create a labeling worksheet of [OBJECT/SCENE]. Add clear leader lines pointing to the key parts, but leave
the labels blank for students to fill in. Include a separate word bank and avoid overlapping text.
008. /DESCRIBE
Copy prompt: Create a picture-description activity for [GRADE]. Show a detailed, age-appropriate scene and add prompts:
What do you see? Where are they? What are they doing? How might they feel? Leave writing space.
009. /MATCH
Copy prompt: Create a matching worksheet for [TOPIC] with two columns: words on the left and corresponding pictures or
definitions on the right. Mix the order, use clear spacing, and do not draw the matching lines.
010. /PHONICS
Copy prompt: Create a phonics practice card for the sound [SOUND]. Show a clear example picture, the target word split
into sound boxes, and three more simple words that use the same sound. Ensure all spelling is correct.
SADDY TECH X
100 AI Image Prompts for Teachers  •  Page 3
PART 2 — WRITING, WORKSHEETS & VISUAL ORGANIZERS
SADDY TECH X   |   Copy-and-paste prompt collection   |   10 prompts
011. /WRITING
Copy prompt: Create a creative-writing worksheet for [GRADE] based on [TOPIC]. Include a colorful scene, a short writing
starter, three guiding questions, and lined space for students to continue the story.
012. /WORKSHEET
Copy prompt: Create a printable worksheet about [TOPIC] for [GRADE]. Include a short instruction, 8 varied questions, clear
answer space, and one small relevant illustration. Keep the page uncluttered and classroom-ready.
013. /CHART
Copy prompt: Create a clear educational chart explaining [TOPIC]. Organize the information into labeled sections with short
points, simple icons, and readable headings. Use accurate facts and a balanced layout.
014. /INFOGRAPHIC
Copy prompt: Design a student-friendly infographic about [TOPIC]. Present 5–7 key facts with simple illustrations, short
captions, and a clear visual flow. Make all text large, accurate, and easy to scan.
015. /COMPARE
Copy prompt: Create a comparison chart for [A] versus [B]. Use two balanced columns and compare definition, features,
examples, and uses. Highlight the most important differences without overcrowding the design.
016. /MINDMAP
Copy prompt: Create a mind map about [TOPIC] for [GRADE]. Put the main idea in the center and connect it to 5–7
branches with short keywords and small relevant icons. Keep labels readable and connections clear.
017. /ACTIVITY
Copy prompt: Design a hands-on classroom activity about [TOPIC] for [GRADE]. Show the materials, three simple steps,
safety note if needed, and the learning goal. Use friendly visuals and concise instructions.
018. /PUZZLE
Copy prompt: Create an age-appropriate educational puzzle about [TOPIC]. Include a clear challenge, neat puzzle layout,
and simple instructions. Ensure the puzzle is solvable and do not reveal the answer on the student page.
019. /PROJECT
Copy prompt: Create a student project guide about [TOPIC]. Show the finished project example, materials needed, 4–6
steps, and a short checklist for presentation. Keep the instructions practical and easy to follow.
020. /QUIZ
Copy prompt: Create a quiz sheet about [TOPIC] for [GRADE] with 10 questions, including multiple choice, true/false, and
short answers. Use clear numbering and enough answer space; place the answer key on a separate page.

100 AI Image Prompts for Teachers  •  Page 4
PART 3 — EXPLAINING DIFFICULT CONCEPTS
SADDY TECH X   |   Copy-and-paste prompt collection   |   10 prompts
021. /DIAGRAM
Copy prompt: Create a scientifically accurate, clearly labeled diagram of [CONCEPT]. Use simple shapes, directional arrows
where appropriate, a plain background, and readable labels. Do not add unsupported details.
022. /TIMELINE
Copy prompt: Create a timeline of [EVENTS/TOPIC] with 5–8 key milestones in chronological order. Add dates, short
descriptions, and simple visual markers. Verify that the sequence is correct.
023. /SUMMARY
Copy prompt: Create a one-page visual summary of [CHAPTER/TOPIC]. Include the main idea, 5 key points, important
terms, and one example. Use concise language suitable for [GRADE].
024. /REALWORLD
Copy prompt: Create a visual showing how [CONCEPT] is used in everyday life. Include three realistic examples, short
captions, and one question asking students to identify another use.
025. /CAUSEEFFECT
Copy prompt: Create a cause-and-effect diagram about [TOPIC]. Show the main cause, connected intermediate steps, and
resulting effects with clear arrows. Use accurate, age-appropriate examples.
026. /CYCLE
Copy prompt: Create a clear educational cycle diagram for [PROCESS]. Show each stage in the correct order with arrows,
short labels, and simple illustrations. Make the cycle easy to understand at a glance.
027. /MAP
Copy prompt: Create a student-friendly educational map of [PLACE/REGION]. Include only relevant, verified labels, a clear
title, a legend, and a north arrow when appropriate. Keep place names readable.
028. /GRAPH
Copy prompt: Create a classroom graph using this data: [INSERT DATA]. Choose the correct graph type, label both axes,
include units, and show values accurately. Do not invent or alter data.
029. /TABLE
Copy prompt: Create a neat educational table comparing or organizing [TOPIC/DATA]. Use clear column headings,
consistent formatting, accurate entries, and readable text suitable for a worksheet.
030. /FLOWCHART
Copy prompt: Create a step-by-step flowchart for [PROCESS]. Use standard start, action, and decision shapes where
appropriate, connect them with arrows, and keep every step concise and in the correct order.

031. /COMIC
Copy prompt: Create a 4-panel educational comic that teaches [CONCEPT]. Use consistent characters, short readable
dialogue, a clear beginning-middle-end, and an accurate learning takeaway in the final panel.
032. /NOTES
Copy prompt: Turn [TOPIC] into concise student notes with a title, key definitions, 5–7 bullet points, one example, and a
quick recap. Use clear headings and avoid unnecessary technical language.
033. /POSTER
Copy prompt: Design a classroom poster about [TOPIC/CLASSROOM MESSAGE]. Use one strong headline, 3–5 short
supporting points, friendly illustrations, and high-contrast readable text.
034. /STEP
Copy prompt: Create a visual step-by-step guide for [TASK/CONCEPT]. Show each step in sequence with one clear
illustration and a short instruction. Keep the same visual style throughout.
035. /ROLEPLAY
Copy prompt: Create a classroom role-play activity about [TOPIC]. Show the setting and list 3–4 roles, each with a simple
goal or line. Keep the situation inclusive, age-appropriate, and educational.
036. /DEBATE
Copy prompt: Create a debate prompt card about [ISSUE] for [GRADE]. Include a neutral question, two reasonable
viewpoints, three evidence questions, and respectful discussion rules. Avoid presenting opinions as facts.
037. /VOCABSCENE
Copy prompt: Create a scene that naturally includes these vocabulary words: [WORD LIST]. Make each word's meaning
understandable from context and add small numbered callouts with a separate word list.
038. /READING
Copy prompt: Create a short reading passage about [TOPIC] for [GRADE], with one supporting illustration, a title, and five
comprehension questions. Use correct grammar and age-appropriate vocabulary.
039. /RUBRIC
Copy prompt: Create a simple assessment rubric for [ASSIGNMENT]. Include 4 criteria and 4 performance levels, with
concise descriptions for each level. Use fair, observable criteria and a clear table.
040. /EXITTICKET
Copy prompt: Create a quick exit-ticket worksheet about [LESSON TOPIC] with three questions: one key idea, one
application, and one remaining question. Leave space for short answers.

041. /BRAINSTORM
Copy prompt: Create a brainstorming mind map for a lesson on [TOPIC]. Add a central theme, 6 idea branches, and small
icons to inspire discussion. Leave some blank branches for students' ideas.
042. /SCHEDULE
Copy prompt: Create a clear weekly classroom schedule using this information: [INSERT TIMES AND ACTIVITIES]. Use a
readable grid, distinguish days and times, and preserve every supplied entry exactly.
043. /SYLLABUS
Copy prompt: Create a visual syllabus overview for [SUBJECT/COURSE]. Organize the supplied units into a logical

Copy prompt: Create a safe classroom science experiment guide about [TOPIC]. Show materials, numbered steps, what to

prompts.title: /WORKSHEET
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /QUIZ
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /MINDMAP
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /FLASHCARDS
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /SUMMARY
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /TIMELINE
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /PLANNER
prompts.text:

checkboxes and a clean layout while preserving every supplied date and task.

prompts.title: /ACTIVITYMENU
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /DIAGRAM
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /SEQUENCE
prompts.text:

blank number boxes, and a separate correctly ordered answer key.

prompts.title: /FEELINGSCHART
prompts.text:

prompts.title: /CLASSROOMRULES

title: 5.3 100 TRADER PROMPT
summary: 100 TRADER PROMPTS For ChatGPT • Gemini • Claude • Copilot • Grok & More Educational use only. These prompts support analysis, planning and learning. They do not guarantee profits
raw:
SADDY TECH X
100 TRADER PROMPTS
For ChatGPT • Gemini • Claude • Copilot • Grok & More
Educational use only. These prompts support analysis, planning and learning. They do not guarantee profits
or replace professional financial advice.
PART 1 • PROMPTS 1–10
1. /Market Analysis
Analyze [asset] using the latest chart data I provide. Identify the overall trend, key levels, possible scenarios and
invalidation points. Do not give a guaranteed prediction.
2. /Trend Analysis
Explain the current trend of [asset] from the chart I provide. Separate higher-timeframe trend from short-term
movement.
3. /Support Resistance
Identify major support and resistance zones on this chart and explain why each zone matters.
4. /Candlestick Analysis
Analyze the candlestick structure in this chart and explain the strongest price-action signals without assuming
future movement.
5. /Chart Patterns
Identify important chart patterns visible in [asset] and explain their typical implications and failure conditions.
6. /Technical Indicators
Suggest which technical indicators could complement this setup and explain what each indicator is designed to
measure.
7. /Moving Averages
Explain what the 20, 50 and 200 moving averages suggest on this chart and how traders commonly use them.
8. /RSI Analysis
Explain the RSI reading on this chart, including momentum, divergence and common false-signal risks.
9. /MACD Analysis
Explain the MACD structure on this chart and what traders typically look for before considering a setup.
10. /Volume Analysis
Analyze volume behavior around recent price moves and explain whether volume confirms or questions the
move.
PART 2 • PROMPTS 11–20
11. /Breakout Setup
Create a checklist for evaluating a breakout of [level], including confirmation, invalidation and risk controls.
12. /Trendline Setup
Show me how to draw and validate a useful trendline on this chart and explain when it should be ignored.
13. /Price Action
Analyze this chart using pure price action: highs, lows, momentum, rejection and consolidation.
14. /Market Structure
Map the current market structure using higher highs, higher lows, lower highs and lower lows.
15. /Entry Planning
Create an educational entry-planning framework for [setup] with confirmation conditions and invalidation rules.
16. /Exit Planning
Create an exit-planning framework for [trade] using predefined targets, invalidation and risk-reward scenarios.
17. /Stop Loss
Explain how to place a logical stop-loss based on market structure rather than an arbitrary percentage.
18. /Risk Reward
Calculate potential risk-reward for this hypothetical trade using entry [price], stop [price] and target [price].
19. /Position Sizing
Show how to calculate position size when account risk is [amount] and stop distance is [distance].
20. /Risk Management
Create a risk-management checklist covering position size, maximum loss, stop placement and daily loss limits.
PART 3 • PROMPTS 21–30
21. /Trading Checklist
Create a pre-trade checklist I can use before entering any trade.
22. /Pre Market Routine
Create a simple pre-market routine for reviewing markets, news, watchlist and risk limits.
23. /Post Market Review
Create a post-market review template for recording what worked, what failed and what I should improve.
24. /Trading Journal
Create a trading journal template with setup, entry, exit, risk, result, emotions and lessons.
25. /Trade Psychology
Explain common psychological biases in trading and practical ways to recognize them.
26. /Emotional Control
Give me a checklist to identify FOMO before I enter a trade and rules for avoiding impulsive entries.
27. /FOMO Control
Give me practical rules to recognize and prevent overtrading during a trading session.
28. /Overtrading
Create 10 trading-discipline rules that are objective and easy to track.
29. /Discipline
Create a simple written trading plan covering markets, setups, risk, entries, exits and review rules.
30. /Trading Plan
Create a watchlist framework for [market] with criteria for selecting and removing assets.
PART 4 • PROMPTS 31–40
31. /Watchlist
Create a screening checklist for finding stocks that match [criteria].
32. /Stock Screening
Create a screening framework for crypto assets based on liquidity, volatility and market structure.
33. /Crypto Screening
Create a forex screening checklist using trend, volatility, liquidity and major scheduled events.
34. /Forex Screening
Explain how swing traders typically combine higher-timeframe structure with lower-timeframe entries.
35. /Swing Trading
Create an educational day-trading workflow from market preparation to trade review.
36. /Day Trading
Explain the main risks of scalping and create a checklist for evaluating whether a setup is suitable for very short
timeframes.
37. /Scalping
Explain options basics using a simple example, including calls, puts, premium, strike and expiration.
38. /Options Basics
Explain futures basics using a simple example, including leverage, margin and major risks.
39. /Futures Basics
Show me how to analyze [company/asset] from a longer-term perspective using the information I provide.
40. /Long Term Analysis
Explain how an earnings report can affect price and what information traders commonly review.
PART 5 • PROMPTS 41–50
41. /Earnings Analysis
Explain how major economic news can influence markets and how to manage event-related uncertainty.
42. /News Impact
Explain how to use an economic calendar to identify potentially market-moving events.
43. /Economic Calendar
Compare the relative strength of these sectors using the data I provide and explain the method.
44. /Sector Analysis
Explain volatility in simple terms and show how traders commonly use it when planning risk.
45. /Relative Strength
Analyze this gap-up or gap-down and explain possible scenarios, confirmation signals and risks.
46. /Volatility Analysis
Identify momentum characteristics in this chart and explain what would strengthen or weaken the setup.
47. /Gap Analysis
Explain common reversal signals and the evidence traders typically seek before acting.
48. /Momentum Setup
Explain how range-bound markets behave and create a framework for trading them without assuming a breakout.
49. /Reversal Setup
Create a trend-following checklist based on structure, momentum, confirmation and risk management.
50. /Range Trading
Explain mean reversion in simple terms and list situations where the approach can fail.
PART 6 • PROMPTS 51–60
51. /Trend Following
Create a backtesting plan for this strategy, including rules, sample size, costs and performance metrics.
52. /Mean Reversion
Turn this strategy idea into precise testable rules that can be evaluated objectively.
53. /Backtesting
Create a trade-statistics dashboard checklist including win rate, average win, average loss, expectancy and
drawdown.
54. /Strategy Testing
Calculate win rate and explain what it means using these results: [wins/losses].
55. /Trade Statistics
Calculate profit factor from these hypothetical results: [gross profit] and [gross loss]. Explain the result.
56. /Win Rate Analysis
Analyze this hypothetical equity curve and explain drawdown, recovery and consistency.
57. /Profit Factor
Explain risk of ruin in simple language and why position sizing matters.
58. /Drawdown Analysis
Create a monthly performance-review template for evaluating my trading process rather than only profits.
59. /Risk of Ruin
Create a framework for evaluating portfolio risk across these positions: [positions].
60. /Performance Review
Explain correlation and show how highly correlated positions can increase portfolio risk.
PART 7 • PROMPTS 61–70
61. /Portfolio Risk
Explain diversification and its limits for a trading portfolio.
62. /Correlation
Create an educational capital-allocation framework based on predefined risk limits, not predictions.
63. /Diversification
Create rules for managing an open trade after entry while avoiding emotional decisions.
64. /Capital Allocation
Explain trailing stops and compare common methods, including their advantages and limitations.
65. /Trade Management
Create an educational framework for taking partial profits while keeping risk predefined.
66. /Trailing Stop
Explain scaling into a position and list the risks of increasing exposure.
67. /Partial Exit
Explain scaling out of a position and how it can affect average reward and remaining exposure.
68. /Scaling In
Create a confirmation checklist requiring multiple independent signals before considering a trade.
69. /Scaling Out
Explain how false breakouts happen and create a checklist for identifying possible traps.
70. /Entry Confirmation
Analyze the broader market context around this chart using only the information I provide.
PART 8 • PROMPTS 71–80
71. /False Breakout
Explain how traders commonly combine weekly, daily and intraday timeframes without conflicting signals.
72. /Market Context
Create a daily-chart analysis checklist for [asset].
73. /Multi Timeframe
Create a weekly-chart analysis checklist for [asset].
74. /Daily Chart
Create an intraday chart-review checklist for [asset] using the timeframe I specify.
75. /Weekly Chart
Create three hypothetical scenarios for this setup: bullish, bearish and neutral, with invalidation for each.
76. /Intraday Chart
Build a hypothetical bullish scenario for [asset] and list what evidence would confirm or invalidate it.
77. /Trade Scenario
Build a hypothetical bearish scenario for [asset] and list what evidence would confirm or invalidate it.
78. /Bullish Scenario
Build a neutral/range scenario for [asset] and explain what would change the scenario.
79. /Bearish Scenario
Review these trading mistakes and group them into execution, risk, psychology and strategy problems:
[mistakes].
80. /Neutral Scenario
Review this completed hypothetical trade and identify what I followed correctly and what I should improve.
PART 9 • PROMPTS 81–90
81. /Trading Mistakes
Suggest objective ways to improve this strategy without changing its core idea.
82. /Trade Review
Turn my trading rules into a short checklist that I can review before every trade.
83. /Strategy Improvement
Create a realistic weekly trading routine including preparation, execution, journaling and review.
84. /Rules Creation
Help me create measurable trading-process goals focused on discipline, risk control and consistency.
85. /Trading Routine
Create a 30-day learning plan for improving my understanding of technical analysis.
86. /Trading Goals
Create a beginner-friendly glossary of 50 essential trading terms with simple definitions.
87. /Learning Plan
Explain [trading concept] as if I am a beginner, then give one simple example and one common mistake.
88. /Trading Glossary
Compare [strategy A] and [strategy B] by setup, timeframe, risk, strengths, weaknesses and failure conditions.
89. /Explain Simply
Create a one-page trading checklist covering market context, setup, entry, stop, target and risk.
90. /Compare Strategies
Create a trading-journal template that I can copy into a spreadsheet.
PART 10 • PROMPTS 91–100
91. /Create Checklist
Create a watchlist template with columns for asset, trend, key levels, setup, trigger, invalidation and notes.
92. /Create Journal Template
Create a complete trading-plan template with clear rules and placeholders I can customize.
93. /Create Watchlist Template
Analyze this completed hypothetical trade from the details I provide and identify strengths, weaknesses and
lessons.
94. /Create Trading Plan
Challenge my bullish or bearish bias on [asset]. Give the strongest arguments against my view and what
evidence would change it.
95. /Analyze My Trade
Create a scenario-planning table for [asset] with possible outcomes, triggers, invalidation and risk considerations.
96. /Challenge My Bias
Perform a final educational review of this hypothetical trade and summarize the setup, execution, risk and
lessons.
97. /Scenario Planning
Help me research and summarize reliable educational information about [trading topic], separating established
facts from opinions.
98. /Final Trade Review
Create a concise pre-trade checklist for [asset] covering trend, key levels, setup confirmation, stop-loss, target,
position size and maximum risk.
99. /Educational Research
Summarize the market information I provide into a clear table of trend, important levels, catalysts, risks and
scenarios. Separate facts from assumptions.
100. /Trade Checklist
Teach me [trading topic] from beginner to intermediate level using simple explanations, examples, practice
questions and a short recap.
SADDY TECH X
100 TRADER PROMPTS • LEARN • ANALYZE • IMPROVE
Educational content only — verify current market data and make your own decisions.

SADDY TECH X • Top 30 Stock Market Prompts
TOP 30 PROMPTS FOR STOCK
MARKET
PART 1–3 • 30 SLASH PROMPTS • COPY-PASTE READY
How to use: Copy any slash prompt, replace the example with your stock/company/criteria, and
run it in your AI tool. Verify current financial and market data before making decisions.
1. /stock-analysis
Description: Kisi stock ka complete fundamental + technical analysis karo.
Example: /stock-analysis Reliance Industries
2. /fundamental-analysis
Description: Company ke revenue, profit, debt, valuation, ROE aur ROCE analyze karo.
Example: /fundamental-analysis TCS
3. /technical-analysis
Description: Stock ka trend, support, resistance, RSI, MACD aur moving averages analyze karo.
Example: /technical-analysis HDFC Bank
4. /screener
Description: Aise stocks identify karo jo diye gaye criteria ko meet karte hain.
Example: /screener P/E < 20, ROE > 15%, Debt/Equity < 0.5
5. /compare-stocks
Description: Do stocks ko valuation, growth, profitability, debt aur risks ke basis par compare
karo.
SADDY TECH X • Top 30 Stock Market Prompts
Example: /compare-stocks Reliance vs TCS
6. /valuation
Description: Stock ki current valuation ko P/E, P/B, PEG aur historical valuation ke basis par
explain karo.
Example: /valuation Infosys
7. /dividend-analysis
Description: Company ka dividend history, yield, payout ratio aur sustainability analyze karo.
Example: /dividend-analysis ITC
8. /risk-analysis
Description: Is stock mein major business, financial, valuation aur market risks identify karo.
Example: /risk-analysis Adani Enterprises
9. /earnings-analysis
Description: Latest quarterly results ko revenue, profit, margins, guidance aur YoY/QoQ growth
ke basis par analyze karo.
Example: /earnings-analysis HDFC Bank Q1 FY25
10. /portfolio-analysis
Description: Mere portfolio ko diversification, sector exposure, risk aur concentration ke basis par
analyze karo.
Example: /portfolio-analysis Reliance, TCS, HDFC, Infosys, ITC
SADDY TECH X • Top 30 Stock Market Prompts
11. /sector-analysis
Description: Kisi sector ki growth, major companies, risks aur current trends analyze karo.
Example: /sector-analysis Banking Sector
12. /ipo-analysis
Description: IPO ka business model, financials, valuation, risks aur key factors analyze karo.
Example: /ipo-analysis Tata Technologies
13. /swing-analysis
Description: Short-term swing trading ke liye trend, support, resistance aur important levels
identify karo.
Example: /swing-analysis Nifty
14. /long-term-analysis
Description: 3–5 saal ke investment perspective se company ke growth drivers aur risks analyze
karo.
Example: /long-term-analysis HDFC Bank
15. /news-impact
Description: Latest company news ka stock price aur business par possible impact explain karo.
Example: /news-impact Reliance Jio tariff hike
16. /red-flags
Description: Company ke financial statements aur business model mein possible red flags
identify karo.
Example: /red-flags Yes Bank
17. /bull-bear-case
Description: Company ke bullish aur bearish scenarios ko evidence ke saath explain karo.
SADDY TECH X • Top 30 Stock Market Prompts
Example: /bull-bear-case TCS
18. /checklist
Description: Kisi stock ko analyze karne ke liye complete investment checklist do.
Example: /checklist Infosys
19. /beginner
Description: Is stock/market concept ko beginner-friendly Hindi mein explain karo.
Example: /beginner P/E Ratio
20. /research
Description: Company par detailed research report banao aur important claims ke reliable
sources do.
Example: /research Asian Paints

21. /intrinsic-value
Description: Stock ki intrinsic value ko DCF, earnings growth aur future assumptions ke basis par
estimate karo.
Example: /intrinsic-value HDFC Bank
22. /price-target
Description: Fundamental aur technical evidence ke basis par short-, medium- aur long-term
price scenarios explain karo.
Example: /price-target Infosys
23. /entry-exit
Description: Stock ke possible entry, exit, stop-loss aur target levels ko risk-reward ratio ke saath
explain karo.
Example: /entry-exit SBI

Description: Mere capital aur risk appetite ke basis par position size ka framework calculate karo.
Example: /position-sizing ₹1 lakh capital, 1% risk

analyze karo.

ka impact analyze karo.

Description: Company ko major peers ke valuation, growth, profitability, ROE, debt aur key ratios
par compare karo.

Description: Current market conditions ke context mein buy/hold/sell scenarios aur relevant time
horizons explain karo.

100 copy-ready prompts • 10 categories • output examples
For teachers, students, graphic designers, creators, businesses and everyone.
HOW TO USE

2. Replace the words inside [BRACKETS] with your own details.
3. Upload a reference photo when the prompt asks for one.
4. Review names, dates, labels and factual details before using the final image.

date errors, so check the output.
SADDY TECH X • TOP 100 UNIVERSAL AI IMAGE PROMPTS
PART 1 — EVERYDAY CREATIVE & PROFESSIONAL DESIGNS
Copy and customize each prompt. The output line describes the kind of result to expect.
1. /professional portrait
PROMPT: Transform my uploaded photo into a premium professional portrait. Preserve my identity, face shape, facial
features and natural appearance. Add flattering studio lighting, a clean elegant background, realistic skin texture, sharp
focus and professional 4K photography quality.
OUTPUT EXAMPLE: A polished studio headshot.
2. /3d typography
PROMPT: Create a stunning 3D typography design featuring the exact text “[YOUR TEXT]”. Use bold modern lettering,
realistic metallic materials, deep 3D extrusion, cinematic lighting, reflections and a premium background. Keep every
word correctly spelled and highly readable.
OUTPUT EXAMPLE: A glossy 3D title graphic.
3. /infographic design
PROMPT: Create a clear, attractive infographic about “[YOUR TOPIC]”. Organize the key information into logical
sections with concise headings, accurate labels, simple icons, illustrations and arrows. Use a balanced layout, readable
typography and a coordinated color palette.
OUTPUT EXAMPLE: A structured educational or informational infographic.
4. /social media post

modern layout.
